item.title: Ohio State reporter calls Jeremiah Smith a ‘petulant child’ for behavior after loss
item.description: Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Devin McCuin (3) high fives wide receiver Jeremiah Smith (4) after a touchdown during the NCAA football game against the Oregon Ducks at Ohio Stadium in Columbus on Nov. 7, 2026. Ohio State lost 41-28. Jeremiah Smith has been one of the few bright spots for the Ohio State Buckeyes during a frustrating stretch, but his frustration boiled over during Saturday’s loss to Oregon as the star wide receiver was visibly frustrated and animated as he yelled toward the sideline in the second half as the Ducks pulled away. While the commentators during the game largely praised Smith’s intensity, pointing to his competitiveness, not everyone around the program was sympathetic. One longtime Ohio State reporter ripped Smith for the outburst, saying that a player of his stature can’t act like “a petulant child,” no matter how badly things are going. Smith’s Frustration Ohio State jumped out to a 14-0 lead over Oregon at Ohio Stadium on Saturday, but the Ducks scored 38 straight points on their way to a 41-28 win. The loss was the Buckeyes’ second straight and third of the season, and head coach Ryan Day said afterward that “there needs to be accountability” for the team’s struggles. Smith went more than two full quarters without a catch during that stretch. Late in the third quarter, with Ohio State trailing 31-14, he finally hauled in a pass and then was seen screaming toward the sideline, as captured by SportsCenter . JEREMIAH SMITH FRUSTRATED Smith was seen screaming toward the sideline as Ohio State trailed Oregon 31-14 late in the third quarter. https://t.co/U15XEpkhDJ — SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) November 7, 2026 It wasn’t the first time that Smith’s usage has been a talking point. After the Buckeyes’ 30-18 loss to USC the previous week, Fox’s Joel Klatt said that Ohio State’s approach with Smith “can’t be your game plan” for a player of his caliber. Smith did eventually get going late, finishing the game with seven catches for 133 yards and a touchdown. But by then, the game was well out of reach. ‘A petulant child’ Jeremy Birmingham, who has covered the program for well over a decade and currently covers the Buckeyes for 97.1 The Fan, wasn’t willing to give Smith a pass for the outburst. “You cannot be the best player in the country and a captain and all of the things that Jeremiah Smith is and go stomping down the field like a petulant child,” Birmingham said on 97.1 The Fan’s Snap Judgments after the game. Smith is a team captain and widely viewed as the face of the program, so his reactions on the field are going to be noticed by teammates, coaches, and fans alike. Of course, plenty of Ohio State fans would argue that Smith had every right to be frustrated, considering how little he was involved for much of the game. And with Day already promising changes, how the Buckeyes use their best player is likely to be one of the biggest questions going forward. Needless to say, it has been a rough couple of weeks in Columbu

item.title: Late release, upright seam, heavy ball: Decoding Mohammed Shami's sorcery
item.description: Few bowlers possessed the ability to strip a batter of his technique, judgement, and ego like Mohammed Shami. The fast bowler from a nondescript village in Uttar Pradesh’s Sahaspur, which literally translates to the “land of courage”, bowled with a big heart, indefatigable spirit, and unmatched skill over 64 Tests. Former England captain Alastair Cook’s dismissal during the Visakhapatnam Test in 2016 was a case in point. Shami bowled a series of outswingers that forced Cook to play away from his body. On cue, he then delivered a perfect inswinger that jagged back sharply to sneak past Cook's defence and cannon onto the stumps. “It’s all in those beautiful wrists,” Shami’s childhood coach Badruddin Siddiqui told TOI . “The reason for his success was that he released the ball late and did not rush through his action. This helped him extract late swing off the track. With those malleable wrists, he made subtle changes at the point of release that batters found hard to pick,” the coach demystified Shami’s skill set. Like S Sreesanth, Shami possessed one of the most upright, God-gifted seam positions in world cricket. Shami was also a bit of a paradox because of the ability to make the old ball skid low while also hurling the ‘heavy ball’ that flew past the batter’s nose. The ‘heavy ball’ — the delivery that pitches shorter and reaches the batter quicker than expected, and hits the bat with extra force despite bowling from a relatively smooth, upright run-up — became Shami’s calling card on numerous overseas tours. The 2018 Johannesburg Test was a classic example: he dismantled South Africa, cruising at 124/1, for 177 to hand India a landmark 63-run win. Shami finished with figures of 5/28, unleashing his trademark ‘heavy ball’ on the spicy Wanderers pitch. — MdShami11 (@MdShami11) At times, he could be erratic even when the conditions were loaded in his favour. But without any warning, he would return with a magical, match-altering spell against the run of play. This streak of unpredictability made Shami irresistible, and it was instrumental in India winning more matches abroad, especially under Virat Kohli’s captaincy. Shami was also a great senior, who passed on his art and tricks of the trade to youngsters. “I learnt a lot of things from him during my time in the IPL. Subtle things like bowling at the death and with the semi-new ball,” Uttar Pradesh pacer Ankit Rajput said. At 36, Shami had been performing admirably in this Ranji season, picking up 14 wickets in his last three games. Yet, the constant snubs and time away from international cricket had hurt him. “He was trying hard to make a comeback. But after a point, he realised he was not going to get another chance in Tests, which is why he chose to retire,” Badruddin explained. “He wants to play the ODI World Cup next year. He has kept that window open,” he added. Shami is India’s highest wicket-taker in the 50-over World Cups, with 55 scalps from 18 games at an impressive average of 13.5. Th

Like S Sreesanth, Shami possessed one of the most upright, God-gifted seam positions in world cricket. But without any warning, he would return with a magical, match-altering spell against the run of play. This streak of unpredictability made Shami irresistible, and it was instrumental in India winning more matches abroad, especially under Virat Kohli’s captaincy. The sorcerer of seam signs off from Tests, leaving a gaping hole in India’s bowling roster. Finding Shami’s replacement would be as difficult as locating Sahaspur on the India map.

item.title: UFC Vegas 124 post-fight show: Reaction to Johnny Walker’s knockout in wild main event
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - NOVEMBER 07: Johnny Walker of Brazil reacts after knocking out Waldo Cortes Acosta of the Dominican Republic in a heavyweight fight during the UFC Fight Night event at Meta APEX on November 07, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC) Johnny Walker was in real trouble, but when you have a fighter as wild and crazy as he is, you’re never out of it. Walker battled back from a deficit to knock out top-10 heavyweight Waldo Cortes-Acosta in the main event of UFC Vegas 124. Because of the short-notice nature of the contest, where do you put Walker’s ceiling in the division? Following the UFC Fight Night card, MMA Fighting’s Mike Heck and Jed Meshew react to the action at the Meta APEX, Walker’s crazy win in the Fight of the Night, and where he could go in his new home at heavyweight. Additionally, topics include Tatiana Suarez’s title hopes following a lackluster win over Virna Jandiroba in the co-main event, Elijah Smith’s breakout performance, other standout moments, Brendan Fitzgerald battling through illness throughout the card, Dana White possibly becoming Donald Trump’s press secretary, and more. Watch the UFC Vegas 124 post-fight show above, or an audio-only version of the show can also be streamed below and on Apple Podcasts , Google Podcasts , Spotify , or wherever else you get your pods.

item.title: Chances of rain in Hamilton on Tuesday: Latest weather forecast for NZ vs IND 3rd ODI at Seddon Park
item.description: Chances of rain in Hamilton on Tuesday: Latest weather forecast for NZ vs IND 3rd ODI at Seddon Park originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Showers are forecast to hover over Seddon Park around the scheduled start time. India could seal the series against New Zealand , but the weather may decide how much play happens. The hourly outlook offers little relief, and a shortened contest looks quite possible. Latest weather forecast for New Zealand vs India 3rd ODI in Hamilton The chances of rain in Hamilton on Tuesday have become the dominant talking point ahead of the third ODI between New Zealand and India, which is scheduled to be played at Seddon Park on 10 November 2026. Persistent showers are expected to move across the Waikato region through the day, and the conditions are likely to have a considerable say in how much cricket the fans eventually get to watch. India hold a 2-0 lead in the five-match series after two rain-affected victories under the DLS method, the first in Auckland and the second in Wellington. A third win in Hamilton would give the visitors an unassailable 3-0 advantage, whereas New Zealand will be desperate to stop the slide and keep the contest alive. The match is due to begin at 3:00 PM local time (NZDT), which corresponds to 7:30 AM in India. According to the forecast, the afternoon is likely to be dominated by cloud cover of around 90 to 95 per cent, with steady bands of rain passing through the region around the time of the toss and the opening overs. Meteorological models also point to a wet day overall, with total rainfall across Tuesday expected to exceed 25 mm. The ground is therefore likely to be damp for much of the match. MORE: List of teams who have lost an ODI series after taking 2-0 lead Hamilton weather forecast for IND vs NZ 3rd ODI at Seddon Park: Temperature, wind and humidity The temperature is expected to stay between 16 and 18 degrees Celsius through the afternoon and evening, although the RealFeel figure is likely to be considerably lower, dropping from about 16 degrees at 1:00 PM to between 12 and 13 degrees late at night. A north-easterly wind of roughly 22 km/h is forecast during the afternoon, easing to about 15 km/h by 11:00 PM, while gusts could reach as high as 46 km/h in the early part of the match window. The UV index is low throughout, with a maximum reading of 1.9 at 1:00 PM, and humidity is expected to climb to around 97 per cent after dark, which will add to the damp atmosphere. Time (NZDT) Conditions Temperature Rain chance 1:00 PM Rain 18°C 83% 2:00 PM Rain 18°C 69% 3:00 PM (scheduled start) Rain 18°C 68% 4:00 PM Cloudy 18°C 49% 5:00 PM Rain 17°C 65% 6:00 PM Rain 17°C 65% 7:00 PM Cloudy 16°C 49% 8:00 PM Rain 16°C 73% 9:00 PM Rain 16°C 77% 10:00 PM Rain 16°C 70% 11:00 PM Rain 16°C 60% Chances of rain interrupting play and a possible DLS finish at Seddon Park The start of the match appears to be the most worrying period, as the probability of rain is around 83 per cent at 1:00 PM and still stands at roughly 68 per cent at 3:00 PM. A delayed start, or at the very least a disrupted opening spell, therefore looks a distinct possibility. The outlook improves only marginally after that, with the chance of rain dipping to 49 per cent at 4:00 PM and again at 7:00 PM, when the sky is expected to turn cloudy rather than wet. These brief windows could allow the umpires to get some cricket underway, in which case a shortened match decided by the DLS method would be the most likely outcome, as it was in the first two games of the series. However, the relief is unlikely to last, because the probability climbs back to between 70 and 77 per cent from 8:00 PM to 10:00 PM, and the threat of a late stoppage or an eventual abandonment cannot be ruled out if the contest is stretched deep into the night. If persistent rain prevents a ball from being bowled, the match will be abandoned, since there is no reserve day in a bilateral series. India would then retain their 2-0 lead with two matches remaining. He remarked during a light-hearted game segment, delivered with the deadpan timing fans have come to expect from him on the field. The joke was set up by stand-up comic Aakash Gupta, who stopped the game to put forward what he described as a historical pattern. His question was directed at Shaadi.com founder Anupam Mittal, and it centred on the idea that a captain who gets married tends to win the World Cup in the following year. On the second attempt, Gupta laid out the examples in full, and the three cases he mentioned are listed below. item.title: Chiefs Trade Pitch Lands $130 Million WR for Monster Draft Package
item.description: (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) Getty TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 21: Garrett Wilson #5 of the New York Jets catches a pass during the fourth quarter against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on September 21, 2025 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Julio Aguilar/Getty Images) Getty One anonymous NFL executive believes that the Jets could wind up trading Garrett Wilson Getty The Kansas City Chiefs must gauge how seriously they regard their own chances of returning to a Super Bowl this postseason, and if after taking a full account the franchise believes it best to do everything in its power to capitalize on one of Patrick Mahomes‘ prime years, then the Chiefs should break the bank to find their QB a legitimate No. 1 wide receiver. Jonathan Jones of The Athletic recently reported that Kansas City is hunting big-name playmakers ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline. “The Chiefs continue to search for wide receiver help,” Jones wrote on Saturday, November 7. “Multiple sources say they’re looking for a big-name receiver — Josh Downs comes up most often — but they are ‘checking on everyone,’ one rival executive tells me. I will be floored if they don’t have someone by Tuesday evening.” Alongside Downs, players like Brian Thomas Jr. of the Jacksonville Jaguars and Jauan Jennings of the Minnesota Vikings are the biggest names that have circulated regularly in trade speculation over recent weeks. However, if Kansas City really wants to swing for the fences, it can make a godfather offer to the New York Jets for Garrett Wilson — a player New York has said definitively it will not move this month. Jets Already Have 3 First-Round Picks in 2027 NFL Draft Getty Wide receiver Garrett Wilson of the New York Jets. It is one thing for a team to say it won’t trade a top player, but surprises do happen when another franchise comes in with an offer too hard to ignore. The Jets already have three first-round picks in 2027, their own as well as one from the Indianapolis Colts and another from the Dallas Cowboys. Were the draft today, New York would pick fourth, sixth and tenth in the opening round, per Tankathon . That kind of capital affords the Jets plenty of leverage in any trade negotiations over the coming days, because even if they package two firsts to get their quarterback of the future next April, they still have another top-10 selection to fill a position of need. However, adding a second-rounder from the Chiefs in 2027 and another first in 2028, which would give New York two firsts in the draft two years from now, might prove enticing. (Photo by Julio Aguilar/Getty Images) Getty One anonymous NFL executive believes that the Jets could wind up trading Garrett Wilson Getty The Kansas City Chiefs must gauge how seriously they regard their own chances of returning to a Super Bowl this postseason, and if after taking a full account the franchise believes it best to do everything in its power to capitalize on one of Patrick Mahomes‘ prime years, then the Chiefs should break the bank to find their QB a legitimate No. 1 wide receiver. Jonathan Jones of The Athletic recently reported that Kansas City is hunting big-name playmakers ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline. “The Chiefs continue to search for wide receiver help,” Jones wrote on Saturday, November 7. “Multiple sources say they’re looking for a big-name receiver — Josh Downs comes up most often — but they are ‘checking on everyone,’ one rival executive tells me. I will be floored if they don’t have someone by Tuesday evening.” Alongside Downs, players like Brian Thomas Jr. of the Jacksonville Jaguars and Jauan Jennings of the Minnesota Vikings are the biggest names that have circulated regularly in trade speculation over recent weeks. However, if Kansas City really wants to swing for the fences, it can make a godfather offer to the New York Jets for Garrett Wilson — a player New York has said definitively it will not move this month. Jets Already Have 3 First-Round Picks in 2027 NFL Draft Getty Wide receiver Garrett Wilson of the New York Jets. It is one thing for a team to say it won’t trade a top player, but surprises do happen when another franchise comes in with an offer too hard to ignore. The Jets already have three first-round picks in 2027, their own as well as one from the Indianapolis Colts and another from the Dallas Cowboys. Were the draft today, New York would pick fourth, sixth and tenth in the opening round, per Tankathon . That kind of capital affords the Jets plenty of leverage in any trade negotiations over the coming days, because even if they package two firsts to get their quarterback of the future next April, they still have another top-10 selection to fill a position of need. However, adding a second-rounder from the Chiefs in 2027 and another first in 2028, which would give New York two firsts in the draft two years from now, might prove enticing. Garrett Wilson Could Serve as Patrick Mahomes’ Top Wide Receiver for Years to Come Getty New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson. It is a long shot on Kansas City’s side, even if the team is willing to put up a first/second-round pick combo, regardless of the year(s) of conveyance. Still, it is a phone call the Chiefs should make, even after the following report from ESPN’s Adam Schefter on October 31. “One well-placed source told ESPN this weekend that there is ‘no way’ the Jets will trade Wilson by the NFL’s Nov. 10 trade deadline, despite any interest from other teams,” Schefter wrote . Wilson is playing on a $130 million contract that runs through the 2030 campaign. He turned 26 years old in July and has amassed 358 catches for 4,171 yards and 21 TDs across 66 games played, including 61 starts. Wilson has accomplished all of that despite regularly poor play from the quarterback position over his five-year NFL career. He has never made a Pro Bowl or an All-Pro team, though Wilson was the AP Offensive Rookie of the Year in 2022. item.title: Shavkat Rakhmonov Suffers Another Knee Injury, UFC Comeback Pushed Back to June 2027
item.description: Shavkat Rakhmonov just can’t seem to catch a break. The undefeated Kazakh welterweight, who boasts a perfect 19-0 record, was expected to make his long-awaited return in January next year, with Michael Morales emerging as a potential opponent. However, any return plans may now be in jeopardy following another setback in his recovery. According to recent reports from Russian MMA outlets, Rakhmonov has re-injured his knee, potentially delaying his comeback even further. The reports claimed, “Knee cannot withstand strain.” With this latest setback, the earliest projected timeline for his return has now reportedly shifted to June 2027. Russian media reports that Shavkat Rakhmonov has re-injured his knee. His earliest return date can be as late as June 2027 😮‍💨 “Knee cannot withstand strain” (h/t @DovySimuMMA) https://t.co/5xiFxZgUQK — MMA On Point (@mmaonpoint) November 7, 2026 ALSO READ: Donald Trump Offers Dana White White House Press Secretary Role, UFC CEO Responds Rakhmonov has not competed since UFC 310 in December 2024 , when he secured a hard-fought victory over Ian Garry despite entering the fight with a significant knee problem. The 19-0 contender had suffered tears to both his ACL and meniscus. He initially explored conservative treatment through rest and rehabilitation before eventually undergoing surgery on January 31, 2026. At the time, his recovery was expected to take approximately nine to 10 months. Since then, fans have been following his progress through occasional updates from his coaching team. Several clips showed Rakhmonov gradually returning to training, working on his conditioning and even participating in sparring sessions. However, there was already some concern about how soon he could realistically compete again. In May 2026, his manager Daniel Rubenstein indicated that the early prognosis suggested the former title challenger might not be ready to fight until 2027. Despite the lengthy recovery, supporters remained hopeful that he could eventually return to the form that made him one of the most feared contenders in the division. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Verdict MMA App (@verdictmma) Now, reports of another knee setback have raised fresh questions about his future. Recovering from an ACL and meniscus injury is already a demanding process, and another complication could make the road back considerably more difficult. Dominick Cruz is one of the most prominent examples of how recurring knee problems can derail an otherwise remarkable MMA career. Rakhmonov’s prolonged absence has already cost him his place among the UFC’s ranked welterweights. He was removed from the official rankings in February 2026 after spending nearly 13 months away from competition. There had recently been renewed excitement surrounding his potential return after Rakhmonov posted a TikTok hinting at a possible matchup with Michael Morales. item.title: Warriors Vet Georges Niang’s History Of Heated Moments With 76ers
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - MAY 05: Georges Niang #20 of the Philadelphia 76ers celebrates a basket against the Boston Celtics during the second quarter in game three of the Eastern Conference Second Round Playoffs at Wells Fargo Center on May 05, 2023 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Tim Nwachukwu/Getty Images) Getty SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 07: Georges Niang #32 of the Golden State Warriors gets in an altercation with Wendell Carter Jr. #34 of the Orlando Magic during the first half at Chase Center on November 07, 2026 in San Francisco, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) Getty The “Minivan” Georges Niang has only been playing for the Golden State Warriors for a few weeks, but the former Philadelphia 76ers sharpshooter is already matching Draymond Green’s enforcer energy out there. On Saturday (Nov. 7), Niang got into a heated dust-up while facing the Orlando Magic. During the second quarter, Niang and Wendell Carter Jr. were playing physical down low, and Niang held onto Carter a little too long for his liking. The two were gripping at each other’s jerseys while players from both teams flew in to break it up. Georges Niang and Wendell Carter Jr. get into it. Draymond Green helps break it up. Double techs on Niang and Carter Jr. pic.twitter.com/nKUDKAJaei — Underdog NBA (@UnderdogNBA) November 8, 2026 It’s nothing for new Niang, who had some “enforcer” moments for the Sixers as well as against them. Georges Niang’s History Of Heated Moments With 76ers Getty SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA – NOVEMBER 07: Georges Niang #32 of the Golden State Warriors gets in an altercation with Wendell Carter Jr. #34 of the Orlando Magic during the first half at Chase Center on November 07, 2026 in San Francisco, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) Anybody can get it when Niang is fired up. Back in 2023, Niang and his ex-teammate Shake Milton had a fiery moment on the Sixers’ bench when they had a miscommunication on the court. After the game, Niang admitted his wrongdoing: “I was being a bad teammate,” Niang said . “There’s no need to do that on the court. It just didn’t need to happen. I need to get my emotions in check. Some of that, sometimes that stuff is good. (Photo by Tim Nwachukwu/Getty Images) Getty SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 07: Georges Niang #32 of the Golden State Warriors gets in an altercation with Wendell Carter Jr. #34 of the Orlando Magic during the first half at Chase Center on November 07, 2026 in San Francisco, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) Getty The “Minivan” Georges Niang has only been playing for the Golden State Warriors for a few weeks, but the former Philadelphia 76ers sharpshooter is already matching Draymond Green’s enforcer energy out there. On Saturday (Nov. 7), Niang got into a heated dust-up while facing the Orlando Magic. During the second quarter, Niang and Wendell Carter Jr. were playing physical down low, and Niang held onto Carter a little too long for his liking. The two were gripping at each other’s jerseys while players from both teams flew in to break it up. Georges Niang and Wendell Carter Jr. get into it. Draymond Green helps break it up. Double techs on Niang and Carter Jr. pic.twitter.com/nKUDKAJaei — Underdog NBA (@UnderdogNBA) November 8, 2026 It’s nothing for new Niang, who had some “enforcer” moments for the Sixers as well as against them. Georges Niang’s History Of Heated Moments With 76ers Getty SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA – NOVEMBER 07: Georges Niang #32 of the Golden State Warriors gets in an altercation with Wendell Carter Jr. #34 of the Orlando Magic during the first half at Chase Center on November 07, 2026 in San Francisco, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) Anybody can get it when Niang is fired up. Back in 2023, Niang and his ex-teammate Shake Milton had a fiery moment on the Sixers’ bench when they had a miscommunication on the court. After the game, Niang admitted his wrongdoing: “I was being a bad teammate,” Niang said . “There’s no need to do that on the court. It just didn’t need to happen. I need to get my emotions in check. Some of that, sometimes that stuff is good. You say what you gotta say and keep it moving.” Later that year, Niang infamously grabbed at Jaylen Brown’s leg during a playoff game between the Boston Celtics and the 76ers. Brown and Niang exchanged words , and both players received technical fouls. One of the other memorable heated moments with Niang was when Ben Simmons played against the 76ers for the first time since his highly documented holdout and trade. Niang would later admit that Simmons frustrated the veteran sharpshooter, but Sixers fans knew that much when they saw the fire that Niang was playing with against Simmons. After Niang left the Sixers for the Cleveland Cavaliers, he spent some time there before getting traded to the Atlanta Hawks . When the 76ers and the Hawks met in March 2025, Niang got into it with then-Sixer Quentin Grimes. At the time, Grimes was having the best stint of his career, posting All-Star numbers on a struggling 76ers team. Niang took issue with Grimes and wanted to expose the fact that if the stars of the Sixers were on the floor, Grimes would be nothing more than a role player. We’ll see if Niang has anything else in store for the 76ers when the Warriors and the Sixers meet for the first time this season on March 24, 2027. item.title: Georgia’s Kirby Smart reveals the most impressive aspect of win over Ole Miss
item.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Georgia’s Kirby Smart reveals the most impressive aspect of win over Ole Miss appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Kirby Smart ’s Georgia football team made their top-10 clash against Ole Miss look like an absolute mismatch as the No. 2 Bulldogs put a 42-7 beatdown on the No. 10 Rebels. The Bulldogs defense was pitching a shutout against Ole Miss until the fourth quarter, when Shekai Mills-Knight scored a consolation touchdown. However, Smart wasn’t disappointed despite the defense losing the shutout. Instead, he gave them props for sticking to the gameplan . “Great job by the defensive staff. Kids bought into the plan. We talked about sticking to the plan. They stuck to the plan. Did a great job,” Smart said in his post-game interview. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Georgia defense completely shut down the explosive Ole Miss offense, limiting them to just 252 total yards. Trinidad Chambliss had arguably the toughest night of his career, completing just 18 of 34 attempts for only 170 yards with one interception and four sacks. He was also held without a touchdown pass for the first time as Ole Miss’ starting quarterback. On the other side, the Bulldogs offense also delivered a major beatdown. The Georgia ground game ran all over the Rebels, finishing with 295 yards and two touchdowns. And quarterback Gunner Stockton threw four touchdown passes, three of which going to wide receiver Talyn Taylor. After Miami’s loss to Notre Dame , Georgia looks poised to reclaim the No. 1 spot in the AP Poll. And with back-to-back dominant performances against Florida and Ole Miss (15 total points, 504 total yards allowed), the Bulldogs defense is rounding into shape at the right time. The Bulldogs will look to put on another impressive performance when they host Missouri in Athens next week. Related: Lane Kiffin’s move to LSU Tigers doesn’t change luck vs. Alabama Related: Oklahoma’s Brent Venables gives Sooners props for rebounding after ‘blistering’ by South Carolina

item.title: Steph Curry has just broken LeBron James’ record during Warriors’ win over Magic
item.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Steph Curry continues to dominate the NBA even at this stage of his career. At 38 years of age, most players would be in decline, but the Golden State Warriors superstar is still up there with the very best in the league. Against the Orlando Magic on Saturday night, Curry proved that once again with a stunning performance, and he broke a really impressive record in the process. Steph Curry breaks LeBron James’ record Curry was once again the best player on the court for the Golden State Warriors against the Orlando Magic. The legendary American scored 41 points and recorded six assists and six rebounds in his 36 minutes on the floor in the Chase Center. That 40+ point return is his second of this season already, and it takes him past LeBron James in a crazy list. Curry has now scored 40 or more points in a game on 16 occasions since he turned 35 years of age. He was tied with James on 15, but is the outright record holder now. Scoring 40 points a few times in a career is a very impressive achievement, but to do it 16 times after turning 35 is simply absurd. Curry really is ageing like fine wine with the Golden State Warriors, and if he keeps going at the same level, Steve Kerr’s side will have a great chance of going all the way. Up next for the Warriors, who are now 7-3, is a home game against the New Orleans Pelicans. Curry has scored 40+ points against them seven times already in his career, the last of which came in May 2021. We’re sure the 38-year-old would love to do it again on Monday night. Read more: Eddie Johnson angrily fires back at LeSean McCoy over Ayesha Curry kissing scene Stephen A. item.title: Alabama RB Daniel Hill brings out the belt after beating LSU in Death Valley
item.description: Alabama RB Daniel Hill brings out the belt after beating LSU in Death Valley appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Alabama running back Daniel Hill celebrated the Crimson Tide’s 31-13 road win over LSU in Death Valley on Saturday by bringing out the belt and striking a Tigers sideline pad. The celebration came after No. 5 Alabama pulled away from No. 14 LSU to claim a much-needed victory and improve its College Football Playoff outlook. Bama brought out the belt after blowing out LSU in Death Valley 😳 pic.twitter.com/JzNwx1Gige Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — ESPN College Football (@ESPNCFB) November 8, 2026 The Crimson Tide found themselves trailing 13-10 with 2:20 remaining in the third quarter after Tigers quarterback Sam Leavitt helped his team take the lead with an 11-play, 90-yard drive capped by running back Dilin Jones’ 5-yard touchdown run. However, Alabama responded quickly, needing just 2:08 to regain control. Quarterback Keelon Russell connected with tight end Josh Ford for a touchdown after wide receiver Rico Scott produced a 57-yard reception and run to set up the score. Russell tossed three touchdown passes despite playing through an ankle injury. He finished with 206 passing yards, finding Ford for a 7-yard score, wideout Cederian Morgan for a 25-yard touchdown and wide receiver Kaleb Edwards for a 4-yard reception. All three scoring passes came after LSU had moved ahead. The Crimson Tide entered the fourth quarter with a 17-13 advantage before extending their lead. After forcing the Tigers to punt from their own 16-yard line, Russell connected with Morgan on the following play for another touchdown. He later found Edwards for his third scoring pass, completing the 21-point unanswered stretch that put the game beyond LSU’s reach. The Tigers failed to capitalize on their opportunities, going 0-for-4 on fourth-down attempts and scoring only one touchdown on four trips inside the red zone. Leavitt completed 35 of 47 passes for 380 yards but threw an interception to linebacker Luke Metz and couldn’t record a passing touchdown. LSU also managed just 77 rushing yards on 33 attempts. The triumph improved Alabama’s record to 7-2 overall and 5-2 in SEC play, keeping the Crimson Tide squarely in the playoff conversation. The Tigers, meanwhile, fell to 6-3 and 3-3, leaving Lane Kiffin’s team with considerably slimmer postseason hopes. The Crimson Tide have now won 16 of their last 20 meetings with LSU and seven of their previous eight visits to Tiger Stadium. Alabama will next travel to face Vanderbilt on Saturday, with kickoff scheduled for 12:45 p.m. ET on the SEC Network. Related: Lane Kiffin’s move to LSU Tigers doesn’t change luck vs. Alabama Related: Oklahoma’s Brent Venables gives Sooners props for rebounding after ‘blistering’ by South Carolina

item.title: Lionel Messi makes history by retaining MLS golden boot title
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Lionel Messi warms up before the 2026 FIFA World Cup Final soccer match between Spain and Argentina at New York–New Jersey Stadium (MetLife Stadium). (is associated with: «Lionel Messi makes history by retaining MLS golden boot title») Tom Weller/dpa Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the golden boot in consecutive seasons. The 39-year-old drew a blank in Inter Miami's 3-3 draw with Charlotte FC on Saturday but his 26 goals over the campaign saw him finish four clear of Peter Musa and with five more than Englishman Sam Surridge in third. The Argentina great also notched 17 assists to finish with a league-best 43 goal contributions for the season. Messi becomes only the sixth player to win the MLS golden boot twice, adding his name to a list which includes former Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips and ex Everton and Portsmouth winger Preki. Despite Messi's exploits, Inter Miami had to settle for second in the MLS Eastern Conference behind Surridge's Nashville SC. Inter Miami will face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup Playoffs, which they won last season as Messi claimed a second successive MLS MVP.

item.title: Warriors star Stephen Curry leads Golden State to dominant OT win over Magic
item.description: Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Warriors star Stephen Curry leads Golden State to dominant OT win over Magic appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Stephen Curry and the Golden State Warriors just keep finding ways to win. The Warriors outlasted the Orlando Magic 126-119 in overtime on Saturday night at Chase Center, as Curry delivered yet another vintage performance to extend the team’s winning streak to seven games . The two-time MVP was simply unstoppable , finishing with 41 points on a blistering 13-of-19 shooting from the field. He knocked down five of his 10 3-point attempts and went a perfect 10-of-10 from the free-throw line, while also adding six rebounds and six assists. The performance also put Curry in the record books . He now has the most 40-point games by a player 35 years or older in NBA history. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The superstar guard came through when the Warriors needed him most. With Golden State clinging to a 120-118 lead in the final minute of overtime, Curry was still going at the Magic defense, having already reached the 41-point mark, as Golden State pulled away for the win. It was the latest in a string of big nights for Curry during the streak. He dropped 34 points against the Phoenix Suns last Monday and followed that up with 29 points in just 28 minutes in Thursday’s blowout win over the Miami Heat . Curry had plenty of help against Orlando, too. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg continued his impressive start with 23 points on 9-of-15 shooting, along with eight rebounds and three blocks. Brandin Podziemski chipped in 15 points and seven rebounds, knocking down four of his five 3-point attempts, while Draymond Green orchestrated the offense with 13 assists. As a team, the Warriors shot 53.8% from the field and 46.9% from deep, and they dished out 32 assists. The Magic made the Warriors work for it. Franz Wagner led Orlando with 30 points and 11 assists, while Wendell Carter Jr. posted 19 points and 11 rebounds . Tristan da Silva added 19 points, and Anthony Black and Jamal Cain each scored 18. Orlando also dominated the offensive glass with 24 offensive rebounds, but its 38.1% shooting from the field proved costly. The win improved Golden State to 7-3 on the season, a remarkable turnaround after the team opened the year with three straight losses . Since then, the Warriors have not lost a game. Curry and the Warriors will look to make it eight in a row when they close out their homestand against the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday. Related: Bill Simmons boldly declares Warriors star Stephen Curry is ‘so so back’ after OT win over Magic Related: Warriors make record history not seen since 1951

item.title: Steph Curry rides to the rescue, propels Warriors to seventh straight win
item.description: Golden State Warriors guard Stephen Curry, celebrating during the first half of Saturday's game against the Orlando Magic at Chase Center, scored 41 points. (Stephen Lam/S.F. Chronicle) Stephen Curry removed the towel draped over his head, dropped the ice pack attached to his right knee and climbed off his chair to return to the court. The Golden State Warriors didn't need Curry to close some games during their early-season winning streak. They needed him this time. Twice. Curry scored 12 points in the final four-plus minutes of regulation Saturday night at Chase Center, nearly ushering the Warriors to victory. But Orlando's Jamal Cain corralled an offensive rebound and scored with 1.5 seconds left, pushing the game into overtime. Curry and Draymond Green both stayed on the bench to start OT, a nod to their advanced basketball age and the effort they expended all night. They rested briefly, then returned to the court - and Curry added five more points as the Warriors earned a 126-119 victory over the pesky Magic. Curry finished with 41 points - his 16th game of 40 or more points since he turned 35, extending his NBA record - as Golden State (7-3) won its seventh consecutive game, its longest streak since March 2025. Yaxel Lendeborg added 23 points, Brandin Podziemski scored 15 and Green dished out 13 assists. Franz Wagner led Orlando with 30 points. This was Curry's second game this season with 40-plus points. He also scored 44 in an Oct. 28 road win over Minnesota. The Warriors won despite 18 turnovers. They also struggled on the boards: Orlando outrebounded them 57-42. Curry returned with 4:34 left in regulation and the game tied at 96. He promptly channeled his 28-year-old self - remember, he's actually 38 - and scored on an array of long-range shots, feathery floaters and driving layups. In all, Curry went 13-for-19 from the field, including 5-for-10 from long distance. After making a habit of digging early holes in recent games - and then storming back to win - the Warriors jumped ahead Wednesday. They seemed on the verge of blowing out short-handed Orlando, only to see a 16-point halftime lead evaporate in a ragged third quarter. The Magic took their first lead of the game at the 3:23 mark of the quarter, when Tristan da Silva buried a 3-pointer. That seemed to stun both the Warriors and the crowd. Golden State had built its cushion by moving the ball crisply in the first half, repeatedly leading to open shots. The Warriors finished the half with 19 assists on 22 made shots from the field. Golden State Warriors forward Yaxel Lendeborg (1) drives against Orlando Magic center Nikola Vucevic (9) during the first half of a NBA basketball game in San Francisco, Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. (Stephen Lam/S.F. Chronicle) Also notably, Lendeborg found himself with a challenging defensive assignment on Wagner. In all, Curry went 13-for-19 from the field, including 5-for-10 from long distance. After making a habit of digging early holes in recent games - and then storming back to win - the Warriors jumped ahead Wednesday. They seemed on the verge of blowing out short-handed Orlando, only to see a 16-point halftime lead evaporate in a ragged third quarter. Golden State Warriors forward Yaxel Lendeborg (1) drives against Orlando Magic center Nikola Vucevic (9) during the first half of a NBA basketball game in San Francisco, Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. (Stephen Lam/S.F. Chronicle) Also notably, Lendeborg found himself with a challenging defensive assignment on Wagner. The injury-depleted Magic - Paolo Banchero, Desmond Bane and Jalen Suggs all were out - needed Wagner to carry the offense, magnifying Lendeborg's task. He moved his feet well, staying in front of Wagner and often preventing straight-line drives to the basket. Wagner still scored 13 points before halftime, though he didn't go wild as Orlando needed (that came later). So the Warriors built an early 15-point lead, survived a second-quarter flurry of 3-point shots from Jevon Carter (trimming Orlando's deficit to seven) and then stretched the advantage to 57-41 at halftime. It helped when Curry buried a long, contested 3 with 2.2 seconds left before the intermission. The first half also featured another scuffle involving Georges Niang, the feisty reserve forward. Niang wrapped up Orlando center Wendell Carter Jr. on a second-quarter play, when Carter caught a pass near the basket. It was a smart play, but Niang also might have been a tad aggressive in bear-hugging Carter from behind. Carter took exception, Niang didn't back down and the situation quickly escalated. Green jumped to Niang's defense, but the officials swiftly and sensibly gave technical fouls to Niang and Carter and the conflict ended there. item.title: Knicks Player Ratings: Towns And Brunson Dominate In Road Win vs. Cavaliers
item.description: Mandatory Credit: David Richard-Imagn Images The New York Knicks dug themselves into an early hole this season, dropping their first three games right out of the gate. It’s been a slow climb ever since, but they are back over .500 now after an impressive win (109-97) over the Cleveland Cavaliers . Coming off a blowout win over the 76ers last night , the Cavs were in a prime position to build on their momentum with a victory over the defending champions. Instead, thanks to steady hands and consistent scoring from stars like Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns , the Knicks held their ground in the first quarter before eventually seizing an eight-point lead by halftime. As much as Donovan Mitchell tried (37 points on 59.1% shooting), his teammates couldn’t buy a bucket, and it didn’t help that the defense was shutting everything down. Ultimately, while the Knicks did not have a great shooting night either (42.7% as a team), they were much better equipped to handle it with a roster and playstyle that’s easily adaptable. If you look at the box score, the stats will tell you that this game was a two-man show between Brunson and Towns, and that’s not wrong — but there were other players who also played a crucial role, albeit in much more subtle ways. In this ranking, we’ll rank all the major rotation players for this win, including Brunson and veteran center Andre Drummond , who went scoreless off the bench. Jalen Brunson: A+ Game Stats: 31 PTS, 6 REB, 9 AST, 1 TOV, 12-25 FG, 3-7 3-PT FG, 4-5 FT, 34 MIN Jalen Brunson had a pretty sluggish start this season, but he’s finding his groove. Tonight was him at his best, as he set the pace with a constant attack. He was scoring in rhythm (with his usual confidence), making perfect reads on the floor that led to nine assists. Without a doubt, he was the best player on that court tonight, and it opened up a world of opportunities for his teammates. Clearly, the Knicks can still count on this guy to deliver. In fact, this was one of his most complete games of the season so far, and it made all the difference for the Knicks. With the team shooting so poorly, Towns raised his scoring intensity and upped his effort on the glass, putting matters in his own hands. Karl-Anthony Towns: A+ Game Stats: 29 PTS, 13 REB, 3 AST, 2 STL, 11-21 FG, 2-4 3-PT FG, 5-5 FT, 33 MIN With all the noise about his extension , you might expect Karl-Anthony Towns to look checked out on the court, but he didn’t look like it tonight. OG Anunoby: B+ Game Stats: 15 PTS, 6 REB, 2 AST, 1 STL, 1 BLK, 4-13 FG, 3-9 3-PT FG, 4-4 FT, 33 MIN OG Anunoby has emerged as the essential glue guy for this team. While there’s still some debate about his value, his play is essential to their success. Against the Cavaliers, he was launching it from three, finishing 3-9 after 33 minutes of play. Of course, his biggest impact came on the defensive end. His ability to contest shots and close out on shooters helped limit the Cavaliers to 32.0% shooting from three (16-50). Jordan Clarkson: B Game Stats: 9 PTS, 2 REB, 0 AST, 4-5 FG, 1-1 3-PT FG, 0-0 FT, 14 MIN In a game where mostly everyone struggled with efficiency, Jordan Clarkson was the outlier. He made nearly every shot he attempted, and most were unquestionably good looks. In the end, the Knicks don’t ask much from JC, but they are better when he’s hitting shots, and we saw that in action today as his mere presence on the court forced the defense to adjust and spread the floor. Mohamed Diawara: C+ Game Stats: 2 PTS, 3 REB, 3 AST, 1-4 FG, 0-3 3-PT FG, 0-0 FT, 14 MIN Mohamed Diawara had a few good moments out there, but his performance tonight was mostly forgettable. He lacked a certain aggression and confidence, managing just two points in 14 minutes. Still, you can’t judge him too closely given that he’s still so young in such a small role for this team. Against the Cavaliers, he was a team-high +16 for doing all the little, unseen things that help impact winning on every play. Andre Drummond: C Game Stats: 0 PTS, 8 REB, 0 AST, 2 STL, 1 BLK, 1 TOV, 0-1 FG, 0-0 3-PT FG, 0-0 FT, 14 MIN Andre Drummond won’t win any scoring titles in the near future, but the Knicks don’t need him to. They signed him this summer to set screens, grab boards, and block shots, all the things he was doing tonight. He played like a man who truly knows his role and how not to overstep his authority. In the end, his eight rebounds helped give his team a 49-40 differential on the boards. Mikal Bridges: C Game Stats: 9 PTS, 6 REB, 4 AST, 2 BLK, 4-13 FG, 1-7 3-PT FG, 0-0 FT, 31 MIN Mikal Bridges is in the middle of an ugly campaign , but he did show some positive signs tonight. Even as his shooting woes continued, he found other ways to contribute, ensuring that he got some value in his minutes. As one of the Knicks’ most active defenders tonight, he wasn’t totally bad, but failed to meet expectations as a core starter. Landry Shamet: C- Game Stats: 9 PTS, 1 REB, 1 AST, 1 STL, 1 TOV, 3-8 FG, 3-8 3-PT FG, 0-0 FT, 28 MIN Landry Shamet was ice cold against Cleveland, but he was getting the right kind of shots. As the fifth starter for this team, his biggest jobs are to stretch the floor and play good perimeter defense. Tonight, he did just that, but it’s just not enough to stand out, even in a game where efficiency was so low. On offense, he was often invisible on the court, and on defense, he was a total liability. Miles McBride: C- Game Stats: 5 PTS, 0 REB, 0 AST, 2-4 FG, 1-3 3-PT FG, 0-0 FT, 15 MIN Miles McBride got the most minutes of any Knicks bench player tonight, and he didn’t make good use of them. While his defense was respectable, he failed to provide any kind of offensive spark or even so much as an assist to a teammate. Whether it’s a personal shooting slump or a symptom of something greater remains to be seen, but Miles McBride is much better than his performance today reflects.

item.title: West's final playoff spots, East craziness & more from Decision Day
item.description: West's final playoff spots, East craziness & more from Decision Day By Charles Boehm However your club may have fared on the pitch, Decision Day remains undefeated. The 2026 MLS regular season ended with a bang on Saturday, with twists and turns right down to the final minutes in both the Eastern and Western Conference. Out West, three teams stepped up to grab their places in the Audi MLS Cup Playoffs, while three others tasted bitter disappointment as their chances slipped away. The Eastern Conference’s drama centered on seeding, with some late surprises benefiting arguably the hottest team in the league, and others raising troubling questions, even for world-renowned icons. Now everyone can catch their breath as the November FIFA international window unfolds. Pulses then get racing again in less than two weeks, when the Wild Card round kicks off MLS’s most exciting month, culminating in the 2026 MLS Cup presented by Audi final on Dec. 18. Let’s dive into how Decision Day unfolded and where it leads us next. ⚽ 🏆 Think You’ve Got the Winning Bracket?! The Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs Bracket Challenge is now open. Make your picks, build your bracket, and compete for your chance to win. Play Now Real Salt Lake RSL in, Galaxy out The day’s six-pointer of all six-pointers unfolded in Sandy, Utah, where Real Salt Lake and the LA Galaxy faced off, both essentially needing a win to book their playoff spot. Alas, the Galaxy didn’t show up early, falling behind 2-0 before 15 minutes had elapsed and never really grasping the magnitude of the moment. Zach Booth sure did, though: A Luc de Fougerolles own goal kept things tense right up until the final whistle. But RSL held on for a 2-1 win that sends them into the postseason for the fifth straight year, the longest such streak in the Western Conference. They’ll visit the Seattle Sounders in the Wild Card round on Thursday, Nov. 19 (10 pm ET | Apple TV ). The result seals a second straight season of underachievement for LA following their 2024 MLS Cup triumph, despite some extensive shopping in the summer transfer window headlined by Chucky Lozano and Sergi Roberto . Conversely, it’s vindication for Salt Lake, who looked done and dusted after a 13-game winless skid in midseason, yet found their famed ‘xDAWG’ intensity down the stretch despite the loss of star creator Diego Luna to injury. Seattle Sounders FC Seattle, too, had to dig deep, and they also enjoyed a strong start, edging LAFC , 2-1 , before a bumper crowd of 40,171 at Lumen Field after Albert Rusnák exploited the visitors’ playing-out-of-the-back error in the game’s opening minute: The Sounders have now made the playoffs in all but one season of an MLS existence that began in 2009. And while this year’s group seems to possess a lower ceiling than their MLS Cup-winning predecessors, there’s a tenacity about Cristian Roldan & Co. that could trip up even a heavily favored adversary. item.content:encoded: West's final playoff spots, East craziness & more from Decision Day By Charles Boehm However your club may have fared on the pitch, Decision Day remains undefeated. The 2026 MLS regular season ended with a bang on Saturday, with twists and turns right down to the final minutes in both the Eastern and Western Conference. Out West, three teams stepped up to grab their places in the Audi MLS Cup Playoffs, while three others tasted bitter disappointment as their chances slipped away. The Eastern Conference’s drama centered on seeding, with some late surprises benefiting arguably the hottest team in the league, and others raising troubling questions, even for world-renowned icons. Now everyone can catch their breath as the November FIFA international window unfolds. Pulses then get racing again in less than two weeks, when the Wild Card round kicks off MLS’s most exciting month, culminating in the 2026 MLS Cup presented by Audi final on Dec. 18. Let’s dive into how Decision Day unfolded and where it leads us next. ⚽ 🏆 Think You’ve Got the Winning Bracket?! The Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs Bracket Challenge is now open. Make your picks, build your bracket, and compete for your chance to win. Play Now Real Salt Lake RSL in, Galaxy out The day’s six-pointer of all six-pointers unfolded in Sandy, Utah, where Real Salt Lake and the LA Galaxy faced off, both essentially needing a win to book their playoff spot. Alas, the Galaxy didn’t show up early, falling behind 2-0 before 15 minutes had elapsed and never really grasping the magnitude of the moment. Zach Booth sure did, though: A Luc de Fougerolles own goal kept things tense right up until the final whistle. But RSL held on for a 2-1 win that sends them into the postseason for the fifth straight year, the longest such streak in the Western Conference. They’ll visit the Seattle Sounders in the Wild Card round on Thursday, Nov. 19 (10 pm ET | Apple TV ). The result seals a second straight season of underachievement for LA following their 2024 MLS Cup triumph, despite some extensive shopping in the summer transfer window headlined by Chucky Lozano and Sergi Roberto . Conversely, it’s vindication for Salt Lake, who looked done and dusted after a 13-game winless skid in midseason, yet found their famed ‘xDAWG’ intensity down the stretch despite the loss of star creator Diego Luna to injury. Seattle Sounders FC Seattle, too, had to dig deep, and they also enjoyed a strong start, edging LAFC , 2-1 , before a bumper crowd of 40,171 at Lumen Field after Albert Rusnák exploited the visitors’ playing-out-of-the-back error in the game’s opening minute: The Sounders have now made the playoffs in all but one season of an MLS existence that began in 2009. And while this year’s group seems to possess a lower ceiling than their MLS Cup-winning predecessors, there’s a tenacity about Cristian Roldan & Co. that could trip up even a heavily favored adversary. Speaking of which… if Seattle beat RSL in the West's Wild Card match, they’ll advance to meet Cascadia rivals Vancouver Whitecaps FC – whom they upset in the Concacaf Champions Cup back in the spring. Portland Timbers Down in Texas, the Sounders’ old rivals from Portland punched their ticket via a 2-0 defeat of Austin FC , and whatever you do, don’t miss the blistering Kristoffer Velde rocket that sealed it: We reckon these Timbers are playing with house money, considering it’s still early days in the Martí Cifuentes era, and when you have a talented maverick who loves the brightest spotlights like Velde, anything is possible in a knockout situation. Their Round One opponent, FC Dallas – who rallied from 1-0 down to crush the playoff dreams of the Colorado Rapids – should expect the unexpected and be ready to play. Columbus Crew Hell is (almost) Real It ain’t over ‘til it’s over! The old saying is as true on Decision Day as any other matchday, as the Columbus Crew reminded us in the breathless dying seconds of the afternoon’s first time slot. With Orlando City ahead of New England , FC Cincinnati losing to Supporters' Shield champions Nashville SC and the Crew level at Chicago Fire FC as second-half injury time arrived, we were just about set for Cincy-Columbus in the Eastern Conference’s Wild Card round, a tasty, do-or-die postseason reprise of Hell is Real, an elite MLS rivalry. (Their classic 2023 Eastern Conference Final slugfest was one of the greatest playoff games in league history.) But Columbus had other ideas. Ninety-three minutes into the clash at SeatGeek Stadium, a match in which they’d trailed on three occasions, their Spanish Designated Player Brais Méndez turned up at the far post to fire home the winner and send the Crew back to Ohio as 4-3 winners . In a flash, Columbus vaulted from ninth place to seventh, dodging the extra game of the Wild Card – and earning themselves a Round One faceoff with Lionel Messi and defending champions Inter Miami . Let’s hope it lives up to their Leagues Cup Round of 16 barnburner two years ago. WATCH: Columbus Crew provide LATE Decision Day drama Orlando City Grizi Show goes on With the East shuffling, FC Cincinnati will visit Orlando City in the Wild Card on Nov. 19 (7:30 pm ET | Apple TV ). While the two sides finished tied on 46 points, the Lions finished ahead on the wins tiebreaker after they beat the Revolution, 1-0 , posting a rare clean sheet thanks mainly to goalkeeper Maxime Crépeau . For just the second time since mid-August, Antoine Griezmann did not get on the scoresheet, but make no mistake: the Frenchman carries the Lions’ playoff hopes on his shoulders, just as he’s single-handedly resuscitated their season since his midsummer arrival. “We could control what we could today, and it was getting the win,” Crépeau told Apple TV’s Michele Giannone postgame. “Being home in a knockout is a huge advantage, and we know here with our people, we're very strong. “Antoine came in and changed the picture of this club.” HIGHLIGHTS: Orlando City vs. New England Revolution | November 7, 2026 Inter Miami CF Inter Miami , for their part, raised almost as many questions as they answered with their latest Jekyll-and-Hyde display as Charlotte FC visited Nu Stadium. It felt like showtime as the Herons surged to a 3-0 lead before the halftime whistle, with easy corner-kick goals from Ian Fray and Luis Suárez punctuated by a long-distance banger from Rodrigo De Paul . Then the vibes shifted completely after the intermission. A rapid-fire Liel Abada brace soon hauled Charlotte back into contention, and Rodolfo Aloko exploited some poor defending with a 90th-minute equalizer that shocked the house. Despite the 3-3 draw , Miami kept hold of second place in the East thanks to New England’s loss up the turnpike in Orlando. Yet they'll be haunted by two more dropped points at their new home ground, where their record (6W-2L-9D) is actually worse than on their travels. “Sadness, rage, pain – there are so many emotions right at the surface,” Herons head coach Kily González said in Spanish postgame. “It’s also about realizing that we messed up: We took a step backward at a crucial moment. Now, we have to see how this situation unfolds. “I’m convinced – and I know what we’re capable of – that we can get through this.” In essence, Miami’s title defense begins now; everything that’s happened so far is a prelude to the must-win setting of the playoffs. Can Messi & Co. do it again? HIGHLIGHTS: Inter Miami CF vs. Charlotte FC | November 7, 2026 AROUND THE GROUNDS → We’ve known for some time that the road to MLS Cup would run through Nashville; the high-flying Coyotes long ago clinched the Supporters’ Shield and the home-field advantage it bestows. But on Decision Day, Nashville still had one more emphatic exclamation point to place on their superb regular season, as they set a new MLS points record (77) with a 2-0 win at Cincinnati paced by Sam Surridge ’s second-half brace. Not only that, they’ve posted the

item.title: LSU’s Lane Kiffin Places Blame for Brutal Loss Against Alabama
item.description: AUBURN, ALABAMA - OCTOBER 24: Head coach Lane Kiffin of the LSU Tigers looks on during the first half of an NCAA football game against the Auburn Tigers at Jordan Hare Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Auburn, Alabama. (Photo by Stew Milne/Getty Images) Getty On a Saturday with plenty of separation in college football, the No. 14 LSU Tigers had an opportunity to earn a massive win over the No. 5 Alabama Crimson Tide in front of their home crowd at Tiger Stadium. Yet, despite recording 14 more first downs than the Crimson Tide and nearly 200 more total yards offensively, LSU lost 31-13. The Tigers turned the ball over twice and went 0-for-4 on fourth-down conversions, which ultimately proved costly. Lane Kiffin Places Blame for Loss When breaking down why LSU failed to get the job done despite statistically outplaying Alabama in several categories, Kiffin pointed to the Tigers’ struggles in the red zone and on fourth down. “It was a very unusual statistical game, you know, yardage wise 457 to 285 and comes down to red zone and fourth downs,” Kiffin said. “We didn’t make any. 0-for-4 on fourth downs and we got in the red zone more than they did. That’ll give you a problem on the scoreboard when you have a lot of yards and that happens.” Kiffin also gave Alabama credit for the way the Crimson Tide played. “Also I credit them. They did a really good job. Some good stuff with the blitz zero in the red zone and you know disguising it and had some good pick/rub plays that the guys got open and scored some touchdowns.” Lane Kiffin on LSU’s loss to Alabama: “It comes down to red zone and 4th downs. We didn’t make any, 0/4 on 4th downs, and we got in the red zone more than they did.” “They had some good pick/rub plays that the guys got open and scored some touchdowns.” https://t.co/XbrC2ReYdv — The Next Round (@NextRoundLive) November 8, 2026 Looking at LSU The Tigers are now 6-3 overall, which means their margin for error is nonexistent. They’ll need to win out, and even that might not be enough to get them into the College Football Playoff. However, LSU will certainly have opportunities to put together some strong wins down the stretch. The Tigers will face No. 7 Texas next week before wrapping up their season with matchups against No. 13 Tennessee and Arkansas. item.title: Postgame Reaction: Mackenzie Blackwood Gives Avalanche a Chance to Find Their Game vs Detroit
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There’s an alternate universe where Mackenzie Blackwood doesn’t stand on his head in the first period Saturday. While the rest of the Colorado Avalanche struggled through a flat opening 20 minutes, their goalie made 13 saves and kept the visiting Detroit Red Wings off the board. The Avs came out stronger in the second period and made good use of their goalie’s early work. They scored twice on four power plays in the middle frame alone and added two more goals in the third (one more on the PP) on their way to a 4-0 victory over the Red Wings at Ball Arena. Blackwood covered for them early and was eventually rewarded with his first shutout of the season. He made 14 additional saves over the final 40 minutes to finish with 27. “It’s nice to be rewarded,” Blackwood said. “I mean, I thought I’ve been kind of stringing some good games together. Obviously, they’re going to score goals in the NHL most nights, but whenever you can come away with zero, it’s a good feeling.” Colorado’s top guys took over from there. Martin Necas had two goals and two assists, while Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar each added a goal and two helpers. All three scored on the power play, which finished 3-for-5 after failing to capitalize on its first two opportunities. “I think special teams and these little things, they get us going,” Necas said. “You need a little help for the power play, and then you know it brings the momentum on your side.” This season has featured plenty of hot and cold stretches for Colorado. Some nights, head coach Jared Bednar’s club looks like the same dominant team that won the Presidents’ Trophy last year. Other nights, it looks nothing like it. But it would be unfair to lump Blackwood into that conversation. He’s been one of the team’s consistent bright spots this season, even after a couple of rough outings early in the year. Blackwood improved to 9-3-1 on the season, and his save percentage climbed above .900 for the first time all year. He’s now been above that mark in seven of his last nine starts. Saturday’s first period was another example of why Colorado needs him to keep that pace. His performance ensured the Avalanche didn’t have to chase the game from behind, something that’s become all too common in recent weeks. “The first goal is so important in this league,” Bednar said. “I mean, check the stats on any team. It’s not just us, it’s every team that seems to have a really good record when they score first.” Against the Red Wings, Blackwood turned aside 13 high-danger opportunities, seven of which came in the first period. Detroit had plenty of opportunities to take control before Colorado found its footing. “We didn’t have a horrible first period, but like, we didn’t generate a ton,” Blackwood said. “And then as the game went on, second period was great, and third. That hasn’t always been the case this season, but it was Saturday. Colorado drew its first power play just 51 seconds into the period but didn’t do much with it. The next opportunity was a different story. William Wallinder went to the box at the 4:21 mark, and the Avs, despite not scoring, arguably had their best power play of the night. Bednar reiterated that after the game. The top unit stormed the Red Wings and generated shots from everywhere. At one point, goalie Daniil Tarasov made a save and nearly kicked the puck into his own net because he didn’t know where it was. They didn’t find the back of the net on that opportunity. But the next three power plays resulted in goals. The Red Wings got a power play at 6:37, but Logan O’Connor ’s aggressive work on the penalty kill drew a penalty to result in a four-on-four. On the ensuing shortened Avalanche power play, Necas scored from the crease after T.J. Hughes caught Tarasov by surprise with a shot that left the goalie down and out of position. The Avs added to their lead at 12:30 with a vintage MacKinnon one-timer from the left circle. MacKinnon hasn’t had many of those lately, but that one beat Tarasov clean for his 10th goal of the season. Necas recorded his second of the night midway through the third period, batting a rebound of a MacKinnon shot out of the air at even strength. Makar then capped the scoring on Colorado’s final power play, carrying the puck from the point toward the top of the circle before unloading a wrist shot past Tarasov. Makar’s goal came just 21 seconds into the man advantage. Good: Top Guys Lead the Charge Entering Saturday, MacKinnon and Necas had not yet scored in November. Both got on the board last weekend against the Calgary Flames. But since then, MacKinnon had been relatively quiet, with three assists in three games, while Necas recorded a single helper against the Predators after two pointless performances. Both broke out Saturday, and Makar joined them with a spectacular performance of his own. It wasn’t just the points. The way all three moved and controlled the game stood out. MacKinnon, Makar and Necas combined for all four Avalanche goals and added six assists. Bad: Flat Start It felt, at least early, like it was going to be another one of those lethargic Avalanche games we’ve seen too often in recent weeks. Colorado struggled to generate much of anything in the opening period, and Detroit had the better of the play. The Avs were fortunate to escape the first 20 minutes without having to overcome a deficit. Credit to them for rewarding their goalie for keeping them in it and finding a way out of that early rut. But the start was concerning, particularly given how often this team has put itself in a hole lately. Related Headlines Postgame Reaction: The Avalanche’s Process Is Being Put to the Test Postgame Reaction: There’s No Excusing These Avalanche Performances Postgame Reaction: Avalanche Responded in More Ways Than One Against Chicago Read more at Colorado Hockey Now

item.title: Nations Championship schedule, results, kick-off times and how to watch
item.description: Rugby’s Nations Championship bursts back into life as the inaugural edition comes to a conclusion in a busy November. The new competition pits the Six Nations sides against the four Rugby Championship competitors, plus Japan and Fiji, across six matches split evenly across the July and November Test windows. The results of those games will determine each of the 12 teams’ seedings for the finals weekend at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium , with six matches contested over two days and both team and hemisphere silverware up for grabs. Each entrant will be matched against the equivalent qualifier from the other pool to decide overall placings at the conclusion of a busy year of international action. France and South Africa currently top the two pools, with New Zealand also unbeaten and level on points with the Springboks. Here’s the full competition schedule, and how it will all work: What is the Nations Championship? Announced during the 2023 Rugby World Cup, the new competition will be held every other year and replaces the traditional summer tours and Autumn Nations Series. It is designed to add context to the international calendar, with Fiji and Japan invited to join the Six Nations and Rugby Championship sides to form a top 12. Promotion and relegation is planned for the future with the second-tier Nations Cup, though will not take place in 2026. The entrants are: Northern Hemisphere : France, Ireland, Scotland, Italy, England, Wales. Southern Hemisphere: South Africa, New Zealand, Argentina, Australia, Fiji, Japan. What about the finals weekend? The first finals weekend will be held at Twickenham on the last weekend (27 to 29) of November. Three days of double-headers will be held at the ground, with the first-placed finisher of the Six Nations sides meeting whoever tops the other pool, and so on and so forth down the rankings. The winner of that marquee match will lift the first Nations Championship trophy, while whichever hemisphere – a term used loosely with Japan included in the “southern” section and Fiji hosting their games in the United Kingdom – wins more final matches will also be crowned. The 1st vs 1st match is worth two points, with all other matches in the finals weekend worth one. How can I watch it? Viewers in the United Kingdom will be able to watch every game on ITV after the free-to-air broadcaster struck a deal to show the competition. item.title: SEC football power rankings after separation Saturday in Week 10
item.description: All 16 SEC teams played in Week 10. All of the top eight teams in the standings played against each other. Most notably, the Georgia Bulldogs thumped the Ole Miss Rebels 42-7 on the road. Georgia looks like the best team in the country while Ole Miss' College Football Playoff hopes suffered a major blow. Georgia is the top team in our power rankings. After Georgia in our power rankings is the Texas Longhorns , who earned a big 34-20 road win over the Missouri Tigers in a game that featured two teams with playoff aspirations. Missouri goes on the road to play Georgia next week. The Tennessee Volunteers delivered at home and beat the Kentucky Wildcats 34-6. Kentucky was actually tied with Georgia atop the SEC standings entering Week 10. However, the Wildcats did not look like an SEC championship contender against Tennessee, who has gone under the radar. The Alabama Crimson Tide continue to have a perfect record against coach Lane Kiffin. Alabama used a strong performance from its defense to dispatch LSU in a big road win for the Crimson Tide. Alabama's red zone defense looked particularly strong. The Crimson Tide justified their loft No. 5 ranking. Alabama, Kentucky, Tennessee and Texas all have two losses in conference play while Georgia has just one. Every other SEC team has at least three losses. Georgia is looking like a lock to make the SEC championship, while the Bulldogs' most likely opponent is up in the air with Alabama having a good chance to advance. Oklahoma notched a 23-7 road win over Florida, who suddenly is having offensive woes (although Florida has played two great defenses over the past two weeks). Vanderbilt beat Mississippi State 25-23 in a battle of two of the SEC's worst teams. Auburn beat Arkansas 26-23 in another less notable SEC contest. SEC football power rankings after Week 10 Georgia Bulldogs (8-1) Texas Longhorns (7-2) Tennessee Volunteers (7-2) Alabama Crimson Tide (7-2) Ole Miss Rebels (6-3) LSU Tigers (6-3) Kentucky Wildcats (7-2) Missouri Tigers (6-3) South Carolina Gamecocks (6-3) Oklahoma Sooners (5-4) Florida Gators (5-4) Auburn Tigers (5-4) Texas A&M Aggies (4-5) Vanderbilt Commodores (4-5) Mississippi State Bulldogs (4-5) Arkansas Razorbacks (3-6) Follow UGA Wire on Instagram , Facebook , X (formerly Twitter) or Threads for more Georgia football coverage! This article originally appeared on UGA Wire: SEC football power rankings after separation Saturday in Week 10

item.title: ‘I Think We Found The Problem With Your Argument,’ ‘Wrap This Up’ — NFL Fans Push Back as 2-Time Patriots Champ Takes a Shot At Travis Kelce
item.description: Oct 25, 2026; Seattle, Washington, USA; Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce (87) walks off the field after a loss against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field. © Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images Rob Gronkowski’s red-jacket day in Foxborough belonged to one tight end, but a comparison from a former teammate pulled another one into the conversation. Gronkowski became the 38th member of the Patriots Hall of Fame on Saturday. The same day, former Patriots linebacker Rob Ninkovich compared him with Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce, in a comparison that left many fans asking why Kelce was the topic of conversation on such a big night for Gronkowski. 2-Time Patriots Champ Takes a Shot At Travis Kelce Ninkovich, one of the former teammates who took part in the ceremony, kept his tribute simple. “Like everyone up here said, it made everybody better to have Rob on the field. Practices were harder than the games. So, thank you, congratulations. We love you.” He then measured Gronkowski against Kelce: “[Travis] Kelce and [Rob Gronkowski] don’t even come close. He’s a receiver, and this guy is a tight end.” One fan went straight at the second half of Ninkovich’s line. “If your argument against a tight end is that he’s too good at receiving, I think we found the problem with your argument.” Others pointed to the timing, since the comparison came on a day built around Gronkowski. “The fact that Kelce is getting mentioned at Gronk’s HoF induction kinda disproves Rob’s point,” a fan wrote. IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator This fan also made the same point about the setting: “At Gronk’s induction ceremony and they still thinking of Kelce, can’t make it up lmao.” Another fan treated the debate as one already settled: “We had this discussion; wrap this up.” This fan borrowed Ninkovich’s phrasing to make a different case: “You’re right! It’s not even close! One is 37 years old, getting inducted into the HoF after being retired for 5 years. The other is 37 years old, getting ready to play a game tomorrow!” Gronkowski actually last played in 2021 and announced his final retirement in June 2022 Notably, the ceremony drew more than 1,000 fans to Patriot Place Plaza on a rainy afternoon. Gronkowski, who beat Adam Vinatieri and Logan Mankins in the fan vote, didn’t hide what the day meant to him. “This honor today means everything to me. The hard work, the injuries, the surgeries, the good times, the difficult times, it’s all worth it to me now.” Drafted out of Arizona in the second round in 2010, Gronkowski played nine seasons for New England, winning three Super Bowls there and a fourth later in Tampa Bay. With the Patriots, he caught 521 passes for 7,861 yards and 79 touchdowns in the regular season, plus 81 catches for 1,163 yards and 12 touchdowns in the playoffs.
