item.title: Alabama QB Keelon Russell Makes Blunt Personal Admission on New Injury After LSU Game
item.description: BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA - NOVEMBER 07: Keelon Russell #12 of the Alabama Crimson Tide waves at fans after a game against the Louisiana State Tigers at Tiger Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) Getty Alabama received a bit of a scare when star quarterback Keelon Russell sustained an ankle injury against LSU. Russell was evaluated in the medical tent and the signal-caller was able to return to the field. After Alabama’s blowout win against LSU, Russell was candid about the injury. The Alabama quarterback indicated that the ankle issue “wasn’t a big injury.” “I mean, when I went into the tent, I know that a lot of heads went down on the team,” Russell said regarding the injury after Alabama’s win against LSU, per 247Sports. “So I felt like just going into the tent, I just had to keep myself confident, keep myself optimistic, keep myself going and I didn’t want to see my team down. “We went into this fight. They knew they needed me. I trust in everybody on this team and those guys just kept pouring into me,” Russell added. “And through the grace of God, it wasn’t a big injury. I was able to step back on the field and just able to give it my all.” Here’s what you need to know about the latest Alabama news after the massive win against LSU. Alabama HC Kalen DeBoer on QB Keelon Russell’s Injury: ‘He Was Not Getting Pulled Off the Football Field’ It will be worth watching how Russell’s ankle progresses ahead of the team’s upcoming matchup against Vanderbilt. Yet, the early signs are positive on Russell’s injury. There is no indication that Russell will be forced to miss time. The fact that Russell was able to continue playing at a high level after sustaining the ankle injury is a good sign. Alabama head coach Kalen DeBoer praised Russell’s toughness after the victory. “Yeah, the kid’s tough. He’s a stud. He was not getting pulled off the football field,” DeBoer told ESPN’s Laura Rutledge immediately after Alabama’s win. “And he went out there and just was steady all day long. You know, played smart, made some plays,” DeBoer continued. “I know he’s going to say there was a lot more out there he could have had because that’s how he is, but I’m proud of him. I’m proud of the team and the way they all fought.” Keelon Russell’s Injury News: What Is the Latest Update on Alabama QB’s Ankle? During his postgame press conference, DeBoer later elaborated on Russell’s performance . The early indications are that Alabama does not appear concerned about Russell’s injury. “Yeah, the guy is tough,” DeBoer said of Russell, per 247Sports. “It doesn’t surprise me because I’ve seen it before with him. The physical toughness and just his determination to be out there on the football field. “It wasn’t just tonight. I’ve seen it throughout the course of the year in different times,” DeBoer added. “And so I thought he just did a great job of staying focused and locked in. item.title: Former Bears 2nd Round Pick Faces Fine For Hit on Controversial QB
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - JANUARY 10: Jaquan Brisker #9 of the Chicago Bears reacts against the Green Bay Packers during the third quarter in the NFC Wild Card Playoff game at Soldier Field on January 10, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) Getty CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - JANUARY 10: Jaquan Brisker #9 of the Chicago Bears reacts against the Green Bay Packers during the third quarter in the NFC Wild Card Playoff game at Soldier Field on January 10, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) Getty A former Chicago Bears safety received a fine of almost $18,000 on Saturday due to a hit he made on one of the more controversial players in the NFL. 2022 second round draft pick, safety Jaquan Brisker, received a $17,911 fine from the league after his hit on Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson last week. Jaquan Brisker Fined for Hit on Deshaun Watson After the game, assuming he would be fined for his hit, the ex-Bears defensive back pre-emptively criticized the flag on him during his new team, the Pittsburgh Steelers‘ 27-6 win last weekend. Jaquan Brisker was fined $17,911 for his hit on Deshaun Watson, who landed in the concussion protocol a few days later. Brisker disagreed with the flag and, preemptively, with the fine. pic.twitter.com/ZJY1y7r2f3 — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) November 7, 2026 “Jaquan Brisker was fined $17,911 for his hit on Deshaun Watson, who landed in the concussion protocol a few days later. Brisker disagreed with the flag and, preemptively, with the fine.” Mike Garafolo reported on Nov. 7. In the clip posted by Garafolo, Brisker made some not-so-friendly comments towards Watson, who remains one of the more controversial figures in the league, having been accused of various forms of sexual misconduct by 27 women since 2020. Brisker Already Criticized Watson After Hit Last Weekend Getty CHICAGO, ILLINOIS – JANUARY 10: Jaquan Brisker #9 of the Chicago Bears reacts against the Green Bay Packers during the third quarter in the NFC Wild Card Playoff game at Soldier Field on January 10, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) “Baby and the quarterback.” Brisker said last week after the game, referring to Watson. “He laying there, you know, crying or whatever he’s doing.” “It is what it is. I hope, I don’t assume I’m gonna get fined, because if you watch it, I mean, I’m hitting with my chest and then I’m off, going to the side, but he had his binky today, so they threw it out there. It is what it is.” Brisker played four seasons for the Bears after being selected with the 48th overall pick back in 2022, each as as a starter. He departed this offseason for the Steelers, with whom he signed a one-year, $5.5 million deal back in March. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Former Bears 2nd Round Pick Faces Fine For Hit on Controversial QB appeared first on HEAVY .

Brisker Already Criticized Watson After Hit Last Weekend Getty CHICAGO, ILLINOIS – JANUARY 10: Jaquan Brisker #9 of the Chicago Bears reacts against the Green Bay Packers during the third quarter in the NFC Wild Card Playoff game at Soldier Field on January 10, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) “Baby and the quarterback.” Brisker said last week after the game, referring to Watson. “He laying there, you know, crying or whatever he’s doing.” “It is what it is. I hope, I don’t assume I’m gonna get fined, because if you watch it, I mean, I’m hitting with my chest and then I’m off, going to the side, but he had his binky today, so they threw it out there. It is what it is.” Brisker played four seasons for the Bears after being selected with the 48th overall pick back in 2022, each as as a starter. He departed this offseason for the Steelers, with whom he signed a one-year, $5.5 million deal back in March. item.title: Justin Allgaier praised for his impact as leader and mentor in NASCAR O'Reilly garage
item.description: Motorsport photo Justin Allgaier is now a two-time NASCAR O'Reilly Auto Parts Series champion , and while he will get plenty of accolades for his on-track success, the driver of the No. 7 JR Motorsports Chevrolet is also a guiding force for the young drivers he is consistently beating for these race wins and now two championships. The ages of the four drivers Allgaier bested on Saturday are 20, 21, 23, and 29. He also has three full-time teammates under the age of 25, making the 40-year-old Allgaier a valuable asset as a mentor for to his teammates at JR Motorsports. Allgaier seems like the bar these rising stars look to to make themselves better drivers both behind the wheel and beyond the track. He is also the one on the receiving end of many of the mistakes as they improve their craft on the track. Allgaier's unique position among the NOAPS garage Justin Allgaier and Jesse Love talk after race Justin Allgaier and Jesse Love talk after race Motorsport.com asked team owner Dale Earnhardt Jr. about Allgaier's unique role in the garage, acknowledging it must be difficult at times to be a mentor when you're also the driver paying the price for many of their mistakes. "We all hear it," said Earnhardt. "Justin mentors drivers that aren’t even on our team. He has to put up with so much crap. All these young guys come to this series, make so many mistakes around him, he has to kind of bite his tongue so many times. Even in our own building, we’ve had races where we get these young guys that come in, you’re trying to shepherd them, tutor them, create an opportunity for them. "The idea in a perfect world is they’re there for a short period of time, then move up. They knock Justin out of the way somewhere. You got to figure out how to have that conversation with them and where they learn a lesson, but also get Justin to understand his role as a veteran within the team, ’cause he’s the constant. He’s the one that’s going to be there next year. "That’s been difficult at times. But he has taken to the mentorship and being the veteran and being the voice in the room. He has taken it really well. I don’t know. I sometimes feel like I wouldn’t have been as good at putting up with some of the hassle that he has to deal with sometimes from teammates over the course of his career in the building. "Yeah, he’s had a fast enough car this year he hasn’t had to worry about it. He’s been ahead of ’em all year. You put enough fast cars on the racetrack, they’re going to run into each other every now and then." item.content:encoded: Motorsport photo Justin Allgaier is now a two-time NASCAR O'Reilly Auto Parts Series champion , and while he will get plenty of accolades for his on-track success, the driver of the No. 7 JR Motorsports Chevrolet is also a guiding force for the young drivers he is consistently beating for these race wins and now two championships. The ages of the four drivers Allgaier bested on Saturday are 20, 21, 23, and 29. He also has three full-time teammates under the age of 25, making the 40-year-old Allgaier a valuable asset as a mentor for to his teammates at JR Motorsports. Allgaier seems like the bar these rising stars look to to make themselves better drivers both behind the wheel and beyond the track. He is also the one on the receiving end of many of the mistakes as they improve their craft on the track. Allgaier's unique position among the NOAPS garage Justin Allgaier and Jesse Love talk after race Justin Allgaier and Jesse Love talk after race Motorsport.com asked team owner Dale Earnhardt Jr. about Allgaier's unique role in the garage, acknowledging it must be difficult at times to be a mentor when you're also the driver paying the price for many of their mistakes. "We all hear it," said Earnhardt. "Justin mentors drivers that aren’t even on our team. He has to put up with so much crap. All these young guys come to this series, make so many mistakes around him, he has to kind of bite his tongue so many times. Even in our own building, we’ve had races where we get these young guys that come in, you’re trying to shepherd them, tutor them, create an opportunity for them. "The idea in a perfect world is they’re there for a short period of time, then move up. They knock Justin out of the way somewhere. You got to figure out how to have that conversation with them and where they learn a lesson, but also get Justin to understand his role as a veteran within the team, ’cause he’s the constant. He’s the one that’s going to be there next year. "That’s been difficult at times. But he has taken to the mentorship and being the veteran and being the voice in the room. He has taken it really well. I don’t know. I sometimes feel like I wouldn’t have been as good at putting up with some of the hassle that he has to deal with sometimes from teammates over the course of his career in the building. "Yeah, he’s had a fast enough car this year he hasn’t had to worry about it. He’s been ahead of ’em all year. You put enough fast cars on the racetrack, they’re going to run into each other every now and then." Eric Warren, the VP of Global Motorsports competition for GM, added that he sees Allgaier as "very valuable to the Chevrolet program as a whole. He really does a lot of the development of the tools, and he sets a great example for the young drivers coming up. And he also does a lot on the Cup Series for us. He’s played that role for a long time now. He really helps as you bring young drivers to know that you can be a veteran and also contribute to the group as a whole." Crew chief Andrew Overstreet agreed, praising Allgaier for his work in the simulator and his mentorship of younger drivers. "I’ve seen him take under his wing a lot of these guys that might be in lower-class cars. He wants to see all of ’em succeed," said Overstreet. "You look back at Dover when we lost that race from the 55 car, that kid [Blake Lothian] had come up to Justin quite a bit to get guidance. That kid was disappointed because he had hurt Justin, but Justin wasn’t mad at him. He took him under is his wing to try to get him better. "It’s great to see the type of person that Justin is to help grow this sport and help these young guys, especially the ones that might not have the opportunity or money to be in the top tier. He wants to see the lower-tier guys be able to do good things." "My job is to leave this sport in a better spot than where I found it" Justin Allgaier wins championship, No. 7 JR Motorsports Chevrolet Justin Allgaier wins championship, No. 7 JR Motorsports Chevrolet Motorsport.com later followed up with Allgaier on that, who first wanted to note that he himself had "great mentors" when he was coming up through the sport, and he remembers how helpful they were in helping him find his way. "You don’t know what you don’t know," said Allgaier. "We say that all the time. It’s really true. There’s so many guys in the sport that have made it to a level of really high, high caliber race teams, opportunities. They just have never learned. That’s not the fault of their own. It’s just the circumstance of it. "Jesse [Love, championship runner-up] and I have had some spirited battles on the racetrack. We’ll just say that. We had some spirited conversations off the racetrack. But it was super cool tonight. Jesse came to Victory Lane. I could see the disappointment on his face, right? Also, he made it very clear that he was going to miss racing with me and he was going to miss the times we had conversations together. "I remember actually sitting here at this racetrack last year and having conversations with Jesse about he was getting ready to make some Cup Series starts. I was an open book. I told him everything he needed to know that I could divulge information. "He left and came back, You weren’t kidding. You didn’t hold anything back. I said, 'no, and I won’t.' Whether they be young drivers, veteran drivers, teammates, non-teammates, my job is to leave this sport in a better spot than where I found it." He finds it strange to think about how some of the drivers he has mentored have gone on to become NASCAR Cup champions and race winners, and he's "perfectly happy" with a driver beating him with the very knowledge he gave them. "I will never shy away from helping these young drivers, especially because I want to see our sport grow to a point of when they leave here and go to the Cup Series, go back down to the Truck Series, when they stick around in the O’Reilly Series, they’re better for it, both on the track and off the track," added Allgaier. "I still want to beat ’em. Nights like tonight are more fruitful when you beat those guys because you know you helped them. It sucks getting your butt kicked by some of these guys you know you’ve helped them along the way. You smile in it, enjoy it. You definitely take a lot of solace in that." Allgaier will now attempt to achieve something never before seen in the NASCAR O'Reilly Auto Parts Series -- winning a third championship in 2027. item.title: Georgia dominates Ole Miss in massive SEC win
item.description: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Georgia dominates Ole Miss in massive SEC win appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Georgia football entered Oxford with a chance to snap Ole Miss’s 16-game home winning streak . Coach Kirby Smart and the Bulldogs obliterated it. And in the process catapulted back into the No. 1 conversation. The No. 2 Bulldogs rolled to the 42-7 trouncing at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium Saturday. And put together that dominating performance on an evening No. 1 Miami went down against Notre Dame. That means the Bulldogs will reignite theories of claiming the top once again. Georgia previously lost its top spot after taking the stunning 27-20 home loss to Auburn back on Oct. 17. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Bulldogs didn’t even need quarterback Gunner Stockton to overwhelm the Rebels through the air. He threw only 15 passes total, completing nine of it. But Stockton tossed four touchdown throws; three landing into the hands of wide receiver Talyn Taylor including the 58-yarder to spark the rout. 58-yard TD strike to Talyn Taylor 💥 📺: ABC pic.twitter.com/4PIjBnfYCb — Georgia Football (@GeorgiaFootball) November 8, 2026 Stockton ended his night tallying 186 yards. Taylor finished with four receptions for 140 yards and scored three times. Ethan Barbour caught the fourth touchdown throw from Stockton, which was a short three-yard connection. Meanwhile, Smart leaned into the familiar run-first identity that’s been a staple of past Bulldog teams. Running back Nate Frazier wore down Ole Miss with 107 yards on 16 carries. Finally, Smart’s area of expertise defense delivered a brilliant game plan that frustrated Ole Miss star quarterback Trinidad Chambliss , who entered this game overhearing NFL Draft buzz. But Chambliss finished 18-of-34 passing for 170 yards and never tossed one touchdown, while getting picked off once. Running back Shekai Mills-Knight prevented the shutout by scoring from eight yards out in the fourth quarter. But Georgia has potentially ended the Rebels’ pursuit of making it back to the CFP. All while Georgia faces moving back to No. 1. Related: Lane Kiffin’s move to LSU Tigers doesn’t change luck vs. Alabama Related: Oklahoma’s Brent Venables gives Sooners props for rebounding after ‘blistering’ by South Carolina

item.title: Who plays on 'Sunday Night Football' tonight? Time, TV channel, schedule, live stream for NFL Week 9 game
item.description: Who plays on 'Sunday Night Football' tonight? Time, TV channel, schedule, live stream for NFL Week 9 game originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . There may be a new favorite in the NFC. The Bears ' offense has been one of the NFL's best behind Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams this season, but after making a huge swing for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, Chicago's defense looked just as impressive in Week 8. Heading into Week 9, the Bears are coming off a win over the defending Super Bowl champions — and they'll get another prime-time matchup, aiming to continue proving why they're title contenders on Sunday night. Here's what's more to know about this week's "Sunday Night Football" matchup. Who plays on 'Sunday Night Football' tonight? Matchup : Buccaneers vs. Bears Location : Soldier Field, Chicago, IL The Bears will host the Buccaneers in this week's "Sunday Night Football" matchup, with Chicago hosting Baker Mayfield and company at Soldier Field. What time is the NFL game on tonight? Date : Sunday, Nov. 8 Time : 8:20 p.m. ET The "Sunday Night Football" game between the Bears and Buccaneers will kick off from Soldier Field in Chicago, Illinois, at 8:20 p.m. ET. What channel is 'Sunday Night Football' on? TV channel : NBC Live stream : DIRECTV | Peacock | Fubo As always, NBC will have the broadcast for "Sunday Night Football," with Mike Tirico and Cris Collinsworth on the call. Alternate streaming options include DIRECTV and Fubo, which offer free trials, along with Peacock. Sunday Night Football radio station Radio station: SiriusXM app and channels 192 (Bears), 193 (Buccaneers) Fans can find the radio broadcast of Commanders vs. Eagles on the SiriusXM app, or in your vehicle on channels 192 (Bears broadcast) and 193 (Buccaneers broadcast). item.title: Tom Wilson to Have NHL Throw Book at Him After Egregious Hit
item.description: WASHINGTON, DC - OCTOBER 14: Tom Wilson #43 of the Washington Capitals is held back by a referee against the Montreal Canadiens during the second period at Capital One Arena on October 14, 2026 in Washington, DC. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) Getty Washington Capitals forward Tom Wilson is likely to have the NHL throw the book at him. Early in the first period of the Capitals’ 4-3 win over the Florida Panthers on Saturday afternoon, Wilson laid a massive hit from him on Florida defenseman Sandis Vilmanis. Tom Wilson receives a five-minute major and a game misconduct for boarding Sandis Vilmanis. pic.twitter.com/lSBSfiG3Da — Sportsnet (@Sportsnet) November 7, 2026 The Washington forward got a five-minute major and a 10-minute game misconduct for the hit. But the situation won’t hardly stop there. The NHL’s Department of Player Safety will likely review the play and determine whether the hit warrants a suspension. As insider Elliotte Friedman noted on the most recent edition of Saturday Headlines, the league is likely looking at the play. The fact that Tom Wilson will get a suspension is not really the issue. The only question mark is the length of the suspension. That situation will depend on how severe the injury was to Vilmanis. Following the game, Florida coach Paul Maurice did not offer much of an update beyond the need to evaluate the extent of the situation. “Probably we’ll have to wait ‘til we get him back to see our guys before we have a real good idea, some imaging and things like that,” Maurice said. Vilmanis left the game and did not return. The hope is that removing him from the game was just a precautionary measure. Tom Wilson’s Suspension History Could Come Back to Haunt Him Wilson isn’t exactly unfamiliar with the NHL’s Department of Player Safety. The Capitals veteran has already received six suspensions during his career, making him one of the league’s most notorious repeat offenders. Some of those incidents have been particularly costly. Wilson received a 20-game suspension in 2018 for an illegal check to the head of Oskar Sundqvist, although that ruling was subsequently reduced to 14 games on appeal. He also served seven games for boarding Brandon Carlo in 2021 and another six games in 2024 for high-sticking Noah Gregor. That history is the most damning evidence here. Under the NHL’s collective bargaining agreement (CBA), repeat offenders can face more severe punishment for subsequent violations. Tom Wilson has already established a lengthy disciplinary record, and the latest incident gives the league another reason to come down hard. The extent of Vilmanis’ injury will be important, but Wilson’s history could make it difficult for him to escape a lenghty suspension. Although, it’s worth noting that Wilson’s past could be enough to condemn him even before getting a definitive prognosis on Vilmanis. But the situation won’t hardly stop there. The NHL’s Department of Player Safety will likely review the play and determine whether the hit warrants a suspension. The only question mark is the length of the suspension. That situation will depend on how severe the injury was to Vilmanis. Following the game, Florida coach Paul Maurice did not offer much of an update beyond the need to evaluate the extent of the situation. “Probably we’ll have to wait ‘til we get him back to see our guys before we have a real good idea, some imaging and things like that,” Maurice said. Vilmanis left the game and did not return. The hope is that removing him from the game was just a precautionary measure. Tom Wilson’s Suspension History Could Come Back to Haunt Him Wilson isn’t exactly unfamiliar with the NHL’s Department of Player Safety. The Capitals veteran has already received six suspensions during his career, making him one of the league’s most notorious repeat offenders. Some of those incidents have been particularly costly. Wilson received a 20-game suspension in 2018 for an illegal check to the head of Oskar Sundqvist, although that ruling was subsequently reduced to 14 games on appeal. He also served seven games for boarding Brandon Carlo in 2021 and another six games in 2024 for high-sticking Noah Gregor. That history is the most damning evidence here. Under the NHL’s collective bargaining agreement (CBA), repeat offenders can face more severe punishment for subsequent violations. Tom Wilson has already established a lengthy disciplinary record, and the latest incident gives the league another reason to come down hard. The extent of Vilmanis’ injury will be important, but Wilson’s history could make it difficult for him to escape a lenghty suspension. Although, it’s worth noting that Wilson’s past could be enough to condemn him even before getting a definitive prognosis on Vilmanis. Capitals Will Miss Wilson Despite His Disciplinary Issues There’s no defending the kind of hit Wilson delivered Saturday. However, there’s also no denying how important he remains to Washington’s lineup. Tom Wilson has two goals and five points this season, numbers that don’t exactly jump off the page. But his contributions extend well beyond the scoresheet. He’s a physical presence, an effective forechecker and one of the few Capitals forwards capable of changing the complexion of a game through sheer intensity. At his best, Wilson gives Washington an identity that opposing teams have to account for. He creates space for his linemates, brings an element of physical intimidation and provides the kind of energy that can swing momentum. Losing Wilson for several games would force Spencer Carbery to reshuffle his forward combinations and find another way to generate the physical presence that has become such a significant part of Washington’s identity. That’s what makes this situation particularly frustrating for the Capitals. Tom Wilson’s aggressive style is part of what makes him valuable, but it can also become a liability when he crosses the line. Washington will have to live with the consequences of his latest antics. And depending on the NHL’s ruling, the Capitals could be without one of their most important players for quite some time. item.title: Notre Dame takes down Miami in major win for CFP
item.description: Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images Notre Dame takes down Miami in major win for CFP appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Coach Marcus Freeman’s Notre Dame Fighting Irish welcomed Mario Cristobal’s Miami Hurricanes to Notre Dame Stadium in South Bend, Indiana and rode 14 second-quarter points to a 31-24 win on a day when Darian Mensah was demolished in a goal-line stand . Irish QB CJ Carr connected with Jordan Faison on a spectacular play that gave the home team a 10-0 lead they wouldn’t look back on. Notre Dame was ranked 11th in the CFP Selection Committee’s latest poll, but knocked off the Committee’s top team after staving off a wild second-half comeback. The Irish win capped a day of upsets among Top 25 teams with the lower-ranked team winning four of seven matchups. Carr staked his claim for the Heisman Trophy with 319 passing yards and three touchdowns while Micah Gilbert added 98 receiving yards and two scores through the air, showing the improved depth of Freeman’s team. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Fighting Irish might have made the CFP with a loss, but they didn’t want to leave anything to chance, as they showed in their huge win over the top team in all the land on Saturday, November 7. The Irish made Jason Sudeikis look good as they fulfilled his pre-game prediction . Notre Dame slightly outgained Miami by a tally of 412 yards to 403 while also winning the time of possession war by a slight margin. Everything came together swimmingly for Freeman’s team as they staked their claim as one of the nation’s best teams, avenging their earlier season upset loss at the hands of the BYU Cougars in Utah. Related: Lane Kiffin’s move to LSU Tigers doesn’t change luck vs. Alabama Related: Oklahoma’s Brent Venables gives Sooners props for rebounding after ‘blistering’ by South Carolina

item.title: ‘Sleep's Going OK?': Max Verstappen Checks In on New Dad Charles Leclerc in Brazil
item.description: Shorter nights for Charles Leclerc as Max Verstappen welcomes him to the F1 Dads' club. (Source: MEGA) Max Verstappen caught up with Charles Leclerc at Interlagos this weekend and asked him something only another new dad would think to ask. In a clip posted on Red Bull Racing's Instagram account, Verstappen was seen congratulating the Ferrari driver on the birth of his daughter, Bianca , and then went straight to how he was sleeping. After Verstappen offered his congratulations, Leclerc smiled and said, "Ah, thank you." Then Verstappen asked, "Sleep's going OK?" and Leclerc answered, "Yeah, perfect." Charles Leclerc and Alexandra Leclerc welcomed their firstborn daughter Bianca on November 3. (Source: MEGA) Verstappen has been through this himself, so he offered some reassurance. Leclerc, running on about an hour of sleep, will find that out for himself soon enough.

item.title: Iowa Football Slowly, But Steadily Keeping Hope Alive
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Iowa just might sneak into the College Football Playoff, as Hawkeyes are playing their best right now. Iowa football has always been able to dominate you on defense and special teams. Related: Is Iowa Football Dr. Jekyll Or Mr. Hyde? This version, though, appears to have a more than capable offense to go with a high-level defense and exceptional special teams. The Hawkeyes put together a pair of impressive scoring drives to take an early lead on Northwestern, prevailing 24-10. The win moved Iowa to 7-2 overall and keeps them within shouting distance in the jumbled Big Ten Conference standings. Hank Brown Has The Iowa Offense Clicking To start the game, the Hawkeyes went on a seven-play, 75-yard drive that took up just under four minutes. It ended when Brown got free for a 21-yard touchdown run. Near the end of the first and start of the second, Brown and Iowa engineered another seven-play series. This one, though, spanned 97 yards and over four minutes. Related: Nebraska Football: Is This The End Of The Matt Rhule Era? Brown hit Tony Diaz on a 24-yard scoring strike to make it 14-0. The Hawkeyes would keep Northwestern off the scoreboard in the first half, allowing just a field goal in the third. The Wildcats put a touchdown on the board in the final two minutes, but by that time, the decision was not in doubt. Iowa also scored 10 points from its special teams to salt the contest away. Braeden Jackson, the son of former NFL player Fred Jackson, went 96 yards on a kickoff return. That came after Northwestern got on the board. Caden Buhr nailed a 52-yard field goal late in the third to make it a three-touchdown game. Efficiency, Running The Football Lead Hawkeyes L.J. Phillips, Jr. has replaced Kamari Moulton as the lead back. Phillips rushed 21 times for 128 yards. Brown was 16 of 21 for 126. He did throw an interception, but made up for it with his rushing score and TD pass to Diaz. Reece Vander Zee caught three passes; Phillips had two and five others caught passes. Cam Buffington continues to show why he is an all-Big Ten performer and possible All-American. He recorded 12 tackles with one for loss, as Jayden Montgomery had nine stops. As a unit, the defense recorded six sacks and eight tackles for loss. Read more at Sportsnaut

item.description: ‘You need desire and intensity … we didn’t match them’ City have now lost three successive league matches Enzo Maresca blamed his side’s lack of desire and the way they were outgunned in duels for a third successive Premier League defeat. After winning their first seven games of the season, Manchester City’s 3-1 loss at Nottingham Forest extended their poor run. Jair Cunha dispossessed Josko Gvardiol to score the opener, then Liam Delap struck twice with muscular surges on the break as Forest won their first home league game since April. “Today I think [the problem] has been general,” said Maresca. “It’s not about one player. In the first half we lost all the duels, all the contacts. Against this team, that is fighting relegation, if you don’t match them … it’s something we need to understand. In this kind of game, if you’re not able to win duels and second balls like in the first half, you struggle. Continue reading...

item.title: There are very few reasons for Unai Emery to leave Aston Villa for Manchester United | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Spaniard may feel some of Old Trafford’s allure when he goes there on Sunday but he is right in wanting to stay at the club with brighter prospects On Sunday afternoon, shortly before 4.30, Unai Emery will leave the tunnel at Old Trafford and walk along the touchline towards the bench. Will he glance around the grand old stadium – faded and leaking though it may be in parts – and think that he could have a part in restoring the club to former glories? Will he look at the home bench and imagine himself sitting there – or perhaps more plausibly, scuttling up and down in front of it – as the first Manchester United manager since Sir Alex Ferguson to land a league title? Perhaps not. Emery is, after all, in “advanced talks” to extend a contract at Villa that already runs to 2029. However frustrating he may find the habitual summer churn, he is good at managing it. He feels the right fit for Villa, and that is arguably the most important factor in determining success. Yet all elite managers share a robust self-belief and there is a paradoxical sense that the worse the situation gets at United, the more appealing the job becomes. Continue reading...

item.title: Martin Ødegaard extends Arsenal lead at top with winner to break Hull resistance
item.description: As most Arsenal supporters would testify, patience is a virtue. They needed plenty during the 22-year wait to be crowned Premier League champions and Mikel Arteta’s side certainly had to retain their composure as they tried to break down a dogged Hull side. They had not beaten Arsenal in 14 attempts since winning on their first visit to this ground in 2008. But with 20 minutes to play, there was still every chance that Sergej Jakirovic’s team could have pulled off one of the shocks of the season. Arsenal had already been denied a penalty just before half-time for a shirt pull on Kai Havertz in the box a week after escaping the same crime against Liverpool at Anfield, in a moment of controversy that could have been the major talking point from this match. Martin Ødegaard had other ideas and the Arsenal captain’s fifth goal of the season was enough to ensure they will go into the international break with a healthy lead over Manchester City. Enzo Maresca’s side are up next here in the league after the international break, with Arsenal having matched their record tally of 27 points from their opening 10 games. The signs look ominous for the rest, even if they were made to work for the points throughout by their opponents. Continue reading...

item.description: It is almost one year to the day when the Leeds manager, Daniel Farke, produced the tactical overhaul many observers believe saved his job. To suggest Farke was under similar pressure going into this game would be a stretch, but without a win in five Premier League games it was not unreasonable to suggest the Elland Road natives were getting slightly restless. Defeat going into the international break would have firmly extinguished what had been a positive start, with eight points from the first four. Continue reading...

item.description: Brentford’s Mali midfielder stood out when he was six and has shone in the Premier League since £39m transfer “When I first saw him, I thought to myself: ‘Who on earth is this player?’ laughs Youness Bengelloun as he remembers Mamadou Sangaré. With the transfer window in full swing in July 2025, the former Manchester City scout and agent was not expecting to come face to face with a “footballing alien”, but that proved the case during a visit to Rapid Vienna’s training ground. A few weeks later, Sangaré moved to Lens for around €5m. “He was impressive and what struck me was his technique and his work rate,” Bengelloun says. That’s more or less the impression Sangaré has made at every club he’s played for, including Brentford, for whom the Mali midfielder signed, from Lens, for a club-record £39m at the start of August. The 24-year-old excelled in his debut against Tottenham a few weeks later , dominating the centre of the pitch and providing the assist for Keane Lewis-Potter’s opening goal, and has featured in every game this season, with Brighton up next. “I gave him his debut for Mali in September 2024, against Mozambique. He made an immediate impact,” says Sangaré’s former international manager Tom Saintfiet. “He’s every manager’s dream player.” Continue reading...

item.title: Chelsea’s Alonso identity still to form in a midfield that remains a problem
item.description: Roméo Lavia’s resurgence is not enough as injuries to other key players such as Moisés Caicedo are proving disruptive Xabi Alonso played for Pep Guardiola at Bayern Munich and was a key figure for Spain when their midfield dominated international football between 2008 and 2012. He does not need to be educated about the importance of control, but there has been a clear distinction between his identity as a player and how his Chelsea side have played. Chelsea’s average possession stands at 47.8% after nine league games. They have made the eighth-most passes in the Premier League and are at their most dangerous on the counterattack. Give them space and they will run riot, but Alonso is yet to see a complete performance and knows they need to improve in midfield. Continue reading...

item.description: Trump Exposed Reactor Core Syndrome very much in play after Democrat landslide – and Fifa’s president may pay a price Oh baby, clamp me in your repulsive mouthparts. Sink your unusually large and venomous fangs into my abdomen. And yes, we are doing this in the White House cabinet rooms, out there in plain sight of the watching world, just a gleaming golden ball between us. But it’s fine. Probably. Now take a sip of those sweet, sweet tiny male arachnoid entrails. An exciting new study was published over the summer into the habits of the Australian redback spider. The research made headlines for its focus on reproductive behaviour, specifically the male’s urgent and very willing engagement in what is known as sexual cannibalism , AKA copulatory suicide. item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

item.title: Thierno Barry double fires Everton to comeback win against Coventry
item.description: The wildly optimistic Evertonian – if such a being exists – could not have envisaged David Moyes’ side fifth in the Premier League with Thierno Barry just behind Erling Haaland in the goalscoring chart when their transfer window closed in calamitous fashion. Yet there they sit, team and striker defying all expectations, following a stirring comeback against luckless Coventry. Frank Lampard endured a torturous night against his old club as Coventry impressed but were refused two strong penalty claims. The Coventry manager felt his team were denied a third time by the video assistant referee for an apparent handball by Barry when edging Everton ahead. Replays were inconclusive. It was the dancing French forward’s second goal of the game and 10th in all competitions this season. He also delivered a fine assist for Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall as the in-form midfielder put his latest England disappointment behind him to seal victory in convincing style. Continue reading...

Tuchel’s inclusion of the younger Bellingham for the Nations League games against Croatia and Spain was further evidence of his shift away from the squad that served him well at the World Cup last summer and towards a fresh dynamic for the mission to win Euro 2028. item.title: Football Daily | You want proper football? Here are the FA Cup first-round ties to look out for
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! For the FA Cup, the early rounds are the juice. The first round proper to be played out over the long weekend is looking, well, proper. And on Saturday at 3pm GMT, a proper time, 31 ties will kick off. No VAR, either. At the stage when the bottom two Football League divisions join the competition, focus remains on those non-league clubs fighting for the honour of the pyramid … John Aloisi winning or choking​ the Chinese Super League , a league so ‘super’ that nine of all 16 clubs in it started the season on negative points due to ‘match-fixing, gambling and corruption’ by the way, and the league leaders not even scoring a single goal in seven hours, is really not something to lay upon someone with a bad hangover. Apropos of nothing, if anyone has any objections to my views on the Chinese Super League, please address any correspondence to: Mr K Mbappé, Madrid (there’s no point two of us getting into trouble)” – Noble Francis. As a man of a certain age frequently being reminded of how out of date I am, the recent readers’ letters regarding technical solutions to shirt-pulling (Football Daily letters passim) concerns triggered distant memories. In late 1991 I was working in the Patents Advice Centre, Newcastle Central Library. A gentleman asked for help to possibly patent an ‘invention’: a football shirt with the seams held together by Velcro, so that any tug would ‘open’ the seam and provide clear evidence to the referee of illegal cloth gathering. As I helped him search for possible equivalent innovations in our paper database (yes kids!) we chatted amiably until I asked how he had come to this seemingly simple yet brilliant innovation. He paused, reddened and began to exhale with elevated pressure: ‘Did you see Arsenal the other night? Tony Adams? Disgraceful. It should never be allowed! In fact, with this shirt it won’t be, and Arsenal will have to learn to defend decently!’ Happy memories, obviously irrelavant to the modern game” – Garren Mulloy. Not fair! Bias! (Picture me, arms wide out, mouth open, eyebrows as high as they’ll go, appealing for reason.) I wrote about skin-tight shirts the other day and you ignored it, publishing a Velcro alternative. Now you’ve published another letter about skin-tight shirts ( yesterday’s letters ), days later. And it gets letter o’ the day! What’s the literary equivalent of kicking the keeper’s water bottle in frustration? I’ve just done that” – Ken Muir. I see that Celtic finally moved up the Bigger Vase charts on Thursday night and started playing a tune when their subs Osmand, Durán and Donovan came on. Too corny but my wife actually laughed at this” – Hugh Jamieson. That was a topsy-turvy Durán Durán show at Celtic, but what else would you expect from a bunch of Wild Bhoys?” – Peter Oh. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Scott Parker’s dramatic West Ham return leaves him struggling for words
item.description: The former midfielder with impressive managerial promotion record began with a thrilling comeback in draw at Cardiff Three days in and Scott Parker has already lost his voice. West Ham’s head coach arrived on Tuesday, watched his side fight back from 3-0 down to draw with Cardiff on Wednesday and was struggling to make himself heard when he met the media on Thursday afternoon. “It’s like in the summer holidays,” Parker said. “You put the flip-flops on for five weeks, then you come back home and you get your shoes on. You’re in a minute, you’ve got a blister on the back of your heel. It’s the same with a throat. I’ve not shouted for a little while. All of a sudden there’s shouting and it’s a bit croaky.” Continue reading...

item.title: ‘In moments of pain, football comes together’: Spain says goodbye to Jesús de Miguel
item.description: Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but the streets of Navahermosa were fuller yet quieter to mourn the Tenerife striker at his funeral The narrow streets of Navahermosa in La Mancha were fuller than they have ever been on Thursday afternoon and quieter too. Silence accompanied the funeral cortege as its made way from the funeral home to the parish church of San Miguel Arcángel carrying Jesús de Miguel Alameda, “Demi”, the Tenerife striker who died after an on-field collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono three days earlier. Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but now they were joined by the game he loved. “We wanted to be close to his parents, his wife and daughter. In moments of pain, football comes together more than ever,” said Luis de la Fuente. The Spain manager did not say much else; there was not much else he could say, not much anyone could. These have been dark, desperate days, days when it was impossible to assimilate what has happened, and there will be more. “We will get through this together but we will need help, professional help,” the Tenerife president, Felipe Miñambres, said. Continue reading...

item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo merely the latest example of a great player who couldn’t let go | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There is no doubt his international career was an incredible one, but it would have been greater still if he had not lingered on the stage so long Nothing, perhaps, is quite so difficult for an elite sportsperson as timing their exit. It’s not easy for any person in any job to weigh the hope of having more to give with the desire not to linger beyond their usefulness, but it’s perhaps particularly hard for top athletes because unrealistic self-confidence is so essential to their success. It takes an almost unhealthy level of self-belief for anybody to make the sacrifices to get to the top, to dedicate themselves to such a precarious vocation, to overcome all the setbacks and injuries and failures. How can someone – whose whole life has been spent assuring themselves there are no odds they cannot overcome – accept that is it, that the time has come to say goodbye? The news that Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football brings with it, inevitably, a sadness. Sadness we will no longer see him skipping past a defender, or burying a neck-thrusting header, and sadness in that the end of the career of any great is a reminder of mortality; all things in time must pass. But there is also a sadness he timed his departure so badly. For at least three tournaments, there has been a sense of Ronaldo holding Portugal back. Continue reading...

item.title: Uefa faces political flashpoint over Sevastopol’s ascent in Russian football
item.description: Promotion to third tier for Crimean club would be clear violation of governing body’s rules amid conflict in Ukraine Uefa and Fifa face a decisive test of their appetite to punish Russia’s integration of teams from illegally occupied Ukrainian territory after FC Sevastopol, from Crimea, won promotion to the country’s professional third tier. Sevastopol were declared champions of group one in Football National League (FNL) 2B, in effect Russia’s fourth division, last month and are believed to have applied for a licence to compete at the level above. Should it be granted and they proceed to FNL 2A, it would appear a violation of Uefa rules that prohibit Crimean clubs from playing in competitions organised by the Russian Football Union (RFU). The governing body would come under severe pressure to extend sanctions on European football’s pariah state, whose club and national teams are banned from competing in international tournaments. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘She can do what Beckham did’: Océane Hurtré making waves at Birmingham
item.description: WSL’s second-highest goalscorer is likened to England legend for her crossing and has earned France call-up At the conclusion of Birmingham’s warm-up, the players quietly and carefully placed their footballs into a draw-string bag. All except one, Océane Hurtré, who nonchalantly chipped hers straight into the bag from about 15 yards. It was an innocuous moment that might have escaped most onlookers at Hednesford Town’s Keys Park but it demonstrated the swagger with which she is playing. To observe the 22-year-old warming up before the 1-1 League Cup draw at Aston Villa last week was to witness a player making skills look easy, taking one touch where others took two and pulling off no-look passes. She is backing up that panache in the Women’s Super League, as the joint second-highest goalscorer with six from the promoted side’s opening eight matches. Only Khadija Shaw has scored more. Continue reading...

item.title: Choke of the century? Chengdu collapse sets up thrilling Chinese Super League climax
item.description: John Aloisi’s players need a point on the final day to seal their maiden title – but their form has dropped off a cliff With four games of the Chinese Super League to go, Chengdu Rongcheng needed just a point to clinch their first title. With one game to go, they still need a point. What was a formality has become a formidable task. The biggest bottle job in Asian football history is very much on and it would be as popular as it would be dramatic. The coach of the Sichuan club, the former Portsmouth and Coventry striker John Aloisi, has seen a 12-point lead over Dalian Yingbo cut to just three before Sunday’s showdowns. Whatever happens, this is a positive and thrilling end to a season that started negatively – literally – with nine of the 16 top-tier clubs kicking off on minus points. Continue reading...

item.title: Has a footballer ever run a marathon faster than James Milner? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: managers sacked after signing new deals, war victims commemorated on kits and the first club website (part II) Mail us with all of your questions and answers It came as no surprise to the Knowledge that James Milner had spent the early months of his retirement training for – and then running in – the New York City Marathon. Yes, the bleep test-loving former Brighton, Liverpool and Manchester City player recorded an excellent time of 3hr 9min 4sec, an average of 7min 13sec per mile. Not bad for a 40-year-old whose physique is more like that of a wrestler than a whippet. “A few years ago, I feel like I could have definitely done sub-3:00,” he said, lamenting his late-career injuries for hindering him. In 2012 we ran a column listing footballers’ fastest marathon times, with the former Leicester playmaker Muzzy Izzet leading the pack on 3hr 22min 36sec at the 2011 London Marathon. That very respectable time has now been surpassed by the Premier League’s record appearance maker, so we thought we had better take a gulp of our isotonic energy drink and run through a few more tales of football’s marathon men and women. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘An absolute afterthought’: the story of the Nigeria women’s team’s fall from grace
item.description: The Super Falcons won’t be at the World Cup and with the prize money going up, they risk being left even further behind It was a historic result in Casablanca – but not in a good way. Nigeria’s 2-1 defeat against South Africa in a playoff in August meant that the Super Falcons are missing out on the World Cup for the first time. It is a crushing blow for the most decorated national side in Africa across both men and women, one that has won no fewer than 10 Wafcon titles . The journalist and lecturer Dr Victor Ademola was in Morocco the day of the defeat. “It was a very difficult evening,” he says. “Some players were visibly emotional while others appeared to be processing what had just happened. I saw players crying as they got on to the team bus while some sat alone or remained on their phones, looking very sad.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Aston Villa, ‘unacceptable insults’ and thin-skinned clutching of pearls
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! When Jamie Carragher appeared as a pundit on Sky Sports Super Sunday, Football Daily was surprised he didn’t have a solicitor sitting alongside him, occasionally jotting notes on a pad or leaning over to give whispered instructions and answer “no comment” to any leading questions about Trey Nyoni starting ahead of Ryan Gravenberch. On Friday night, the former Liverpool defender was subjected to a threat of legal action from Aston Villa, who took such grave exception to some “unacceptable insults” he had rained down on them from his podcast pulpit, that they were ready to call in the heavy legal artillery and stop him from preventing their “ascension in English and European football”. Taking a leaf out of the tried-and-much-ridiculed Nottingham Forest playbook , Villa chair Nassef Sawiris appears to have eschewed contacting Carragher through the usual formal channels and instead cajoled some unfortunate junior comms staffer to make the portentous announcement on their Social Media Disgraces. Continue reading...

item.title: From VHS dreams to San Siro glory: Amorim’s Milan surge puts rivals on notice | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Inspired by the legendary Milan sides of his youth, the manager gave his side a lift with a tactical victory over Inter Ruben Amorim had waited a lifetime for his first Milan derby. As a kid growing up in Lisbon, he supported two football teams. There was the local one, Benfica, whose games he attended so early in life that his father has recalled changing nappies in the stands of the old Estádio da Luz. And the other one that captivated him from overseas. “I remember watching tapes of that Milan team with [Paolo] Maldini, [Franco] Baresi, [Ruud] Gullit, [Frank] Rijkaard, [Dejan] Savicevic,” Amorim told the Portuguese newspaper Expresso in 2017. “My childhood dreams were to play for Benfica and Milan. I’ve fulfilled one. Now I suppose I’ll have to become a coach for the other!” Continue reading...

item.title: Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or party gives way to anxiety-filled hangover for Bayern Munich | Andy Brassell
item.description: Dortmund did not read the script, remaining level on points with the defending champions at the top of the table It was the moment they had all been … not so much waiting for, but planning, pushing and yearning for. In the videos that announce the starting lineup on the giant scoreboard before kick-off, every Bayern Munich player turns to face the camera with their personal salute, greeting or goal celebration, the playful progression from the standard folding of arms. Except on Saturday evening, the No 9 turned around smiling, and cradling the golden trophy. In the midweek DFB Pokal stroll against Magdeburg there had been a salute, the players welcoming Harry Kane on to the pitch with a guard of honour to commemorate his Ballon d’Or victory two nights before. This, however, was the real party, the moment where the England captain’s and Bayern’s successful union and the apex it has reached was celebrated in front of a global audience. There was every reason to believe it would be a full and satisfying victory lap, even in Der Klassiker, with proper competition so often bringing the best out of the Rekordmeister. Continue reading...

item.title: Folarin Balogun takes a first, tiny step toward moving on from a calamitous summer
item.description: The USMNT striker scored his first goal since the World Cup in a losing effort against Paris FC. Could it lead to something more? Before this weekend, the last time Folarin Balogun scored was in the United States’ 2-0 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina at this past summer’s World Cup. In the immediate aftermath, the outlook for Balogun seemed rosy; an ascendant player who could muster a goal in tense games. At half-time against Bosnia, US fans weren’t just wondering how far his team could advance – they were sizing Balogun up against some of the world’s best strikers. But for most of the ensuing four months, Balogun has been in limbo. His breakout World Cup was overshadowed by a red card in that same game against Bosnia and Herzegovina, followed by a scandal of which he wanted no part. Just as it seemed a summer move away from Monaco could get his club career on track, he broke off a possible deadline-day move to Everton after a lengthy visit to the training grounds and a medical he felt was improperly handled. Continue reading...

Just as it seemed a summer move away from Monaco could get his club career on track, he broke off a possible deadline-day move to Everton after a lengthy visit to the training grounds and a medical he felt was improperly handled. item.title: Rampant Salford hint that Beckham’s lofty ambitions are not a pipe dream
item.description: The aim of reaching the Championship looks more realistic for a Manchester club in the shadow of City and United After seven seasons in League Two, Salford City are finally threatening to match the hype brought by their high-profile owners. First it was the Class of ’92 who guided them up through the non-league system into the fourth tier but failed to progress any further. Gary Neville and David Beckham remain, part of a new group that took over in May 2025, with this year beginning to look transformational after securing an eighth straight win, against Exeter, to put them five points clear at the top. The budget has increased, allowing the club to sign a number of players who will feel they are above League Two standard. Striker Macaulay Langstaff arrived from Millwall; the last time he played at this level, he scored 28 league goals in a season for Notts County. Match-winner Will Aimson spent the past two seasons in the division above with Wigan and has dropped down because of Salford’s project. Continue reading...

item.title: How can playing for Manchester City fit into Marc Guéhi’s moral universe? | Barney Ronay
item.description: Club’s predicament raises interesting questions about principles, both for individuals and the Premier League I felt unbelievably ponderous. My head was made of Aztec stone. I realised I didn’t want to be with all these people. Somebody came at me, a huge individual in silver and blue. I fell at his feet and grabbed one shoe. I started untying the lace. He kicked away from me. I got up and walked off. I was exceedingly hungry. Not my words. Also not the words of the Manchester City centre-back Marc Guéhi, despite what you were thinking there. This is instead a condensed quote from the mind of Gary Harkness, existentially curious college running-back and the narrator of Don DeLillo’s great American football novel End Zone. Continue reading...

item.title: A phone-free Yellow Wall: are Dortmund urging fans to be present or policing them?
item.description: It makes sense that sports teams want to keep influencers out of their games. The battle some clubs are waging with their fans, however, is a different dilemma By all appearances, things on the Yellow Wall seemed as they always had been. The stadium announcer hollered out the first names of Borussia Dortmund’s starting lineup and the supporters responded with their last names, tens of thousands of voices bellowing as one. Dozens of black and yellow flags waved over Europe’s largest standing terrace, a mass of faces fixed on the field beneath them. And then Signal Iduna Park, sold out with 81,365 fans, roared when Max Beier’s lone goal led Dortmund to victory over Eintracht Frankfurt last Saturday, putting the home side even on points with Bayern Munich atop the Bundesliga standings. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

item.title: Ian Holloway’s circus: why the manager’s antics are no laughing matter for fans
item.description: Swindon manager has a history of viral outbursts but fans want a united club and manager they can support In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Holloway at his finest. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game. Continue reading...
